# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

### Scope
- **Feature**: Split Payment functionality enabling customers to pay a single order with two cards
- **In Scope**: Split amount selection (UI), amount calculation logic (backend), dual-charge orchestration (PayGate integration), automatic refund workflow (on second-charge decline), data persistence and reconciliation
- **Out of Scope**: Single-card payment flow (regression testing only, not new feature testing); PayGate infrastructure or sandboxing; fraud detection; subscription/recurring payments; loyalty or discount logic

### Objectives
1. Verify split payment calculation is mathematically correct, especially rounding (remainder cent to first card)
2. Verify both charges execute in correct sequence through PayGate
3. Verify automatic refund triggers and completes within 60 seconds if second charge declines
4. Verify existing single-card payment flow remains unbroken (4,000 orders/day baseline)
5. Verify system remains performant under normal load during split payment transactions
6. Identify security, data-integrity, or integration defects before release

### Test Basis
- Feature requirements document (split payment functional spec)
- PayGate API documentation (charge and refund endpoints)
- Existing single-card payment specification
- Payment PCI/security standards (as applicable)

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

| Assumption | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|
| PayGate mock API is complete and available by day 2 of testing; sandbox is accessible Tuesdays and Thursdays only as stated | Required to parallelize test execution without blocking on sandbox availability |
| Split payment feature is built in the backend (API) and frontend (checkout form); both are merged to the release branch by day 5 | Drives test schedule and phasing |
| Automatic refund is triggered via a separate PayGate refund API call, not a native "split charge" reversal | Affects test design for refund verification |
| Development team has capacity to fix defects within 24 hours during the test window | Enables re-test cycles before release |
| Production PayGate account and sandbox credentials are configured in staging environment | Required for sandbox testing on Tues/Thu |
| Test data can be seeded into dev/staging without PayGate; production test cards are available | Allows mock-based testing before integration |
| Single-card payment code path is isolated from split-payment changes (no shared refactoring) | Reduces regression scope and risk |
| PO and stakeholders accept testing and release proceeding based on release-gate cases + sandbox verification | Defines exit criteria |
| No major PayGate downtime or service issues during the 10-day window | Outside team's control; monitoring plan in place to detect early |

| Constraint | Impact |
|-----------|--------|
| One QA tester @ 50% allocation (4 hrs/day for 10 days) | ~40 hours available; prioritizes test design and release-gate execution over exhaustive edge-case testing |
| PayGate sandbox open only Tuesdays and Thursdays | 4 sandbox windows (10/29, 11/4, 11/6, 11/11); integration testing must batch into these slots; mock testing runs on other days |
| Release date: 10 working days from 2026-10-28 → 2026-11-11 | Tight timeline; no extension buffer; dev work must complete by day 5 to allow 5 days for test execution and sign-off |
| Existing single-card payment handles ~4,000 orders/day | System must remain stable; regression testing is smoke-level, not exhaustive |

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Person/Team | Responsibility | Involvement |
|------|-------------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Product Owner** | [PO Name] | Define acceptance criteria, approve feature, sign off on test results and release risk | Weekly status, gate approval, final sign-off |
| **Development Team** | 2 engineers | Implement feature, fix defects, provide PayGate mock, support environment setup | Daily standup, defect triage, code review of test feedback |
| **QA / Test Lead** | 1 tester @ 50% | Write test cases, execute tests, log defects, track metrics, report progress | Daily execution, results reporting, gate verification |
| **DevOps / Platform** | [Platform team] | Provide dev/staging environments, manage PayGate credentials, seed test data | Setup (day 1–2), on-call for environment issues |
| **Payment Systems Owner** | [Payment team] | Advise on PayGate integration, refund orchestration, compliance | Available for consultation, review integration test results |

---

## 4. Communication

| Communication | Frequency | Format | Attendees |
|---------------|-----------|--------|-----------|
| Daily Standup | Every morning (async) | Slack thread or brief call | Dev (2), QA (1), PO (optional) |
| Defect Triage | 2x per week (Mon/Wed) | Ticket review + Slack | Dev lead (1), QA (1), PO (optional) |
| Weekly Status | End of week (Fri) | Email + chart (cases run/passed/failed/blocked) | PO, Dev lead, QA, Platform |
| Blockers / Escalation | As needed | Slack immediate + email summary | PO, Dev lead, QA |
| Test Completion / Sign-off | Day 10 (release eve) | Formal sign-off document (email + ticket comment) | PO, QA lead, Dev lead |

**Document Templates**: Test cases stored in Jira/ADO with format `[TC-NNN]: Title | Expected Result | Actual Result | Pass/Fail/Blocked | Notes | Build Hash | Env Version`

---

## 5. Risk Register (5×5 Product & Project Risk Matrix)

### Risk Scoring Guidance
- **Likelihood (L)**: 1 = Remote, 2 = Low, 3 = Medium, 4 = High, 5 = Very High
- **Impact (I)**: 1 = Trivial, 2 = Minor, 3 = Moderate, 4 = Major, 5 = Critical
- **Score = L × I**: 15–25 = 🔴 CRITICAL | 8–14 = 🟠 HIGH | 4–7 = 🟡 MEDIUM | 1–3 = 🟢 LOW

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status |
|---|----|--------------------|----------|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|-------|--------|
| 1 | R01 | Split amount calculation incorrect (wrong card debits, remainder logic fails) | Product | 3 | 5 | **15** | 🔴 CRITICAL | Unit test every split scenario (100, 101, 1000, 10001 cents); boundary value analysis; manual review of calculation logic before day 3 | Dev/QA | Active |
| 2 | R02 | Refund does not trigger or exceeds 60-second window when second charge declines | Product | 2 | 5 | **10** | 🟠 HIGH | Implement refund timer with explicit logging; mock PayGate refund API to return configurable latencies; E2E test with 3-second, 30-second, 59-second delays; code review of refund state machine | Dev/QA | Active |
| 3 | R03 | Single-card payment broken by split-payment changes (regression failure affecting 4,000/day baseline) | Product | 2 | 5 | **10** | 🟠 HIGH | Isolate split logic to new code path; run existing single-card payment unit + E2E smoke tests before and after merge; mock PayGate and execute happy-path single-card flow as part of release gate | QA/Dev | Active |
| 4 | R04 | Race condition: both charges decline, both succeed, or only first charges when network splits | Product | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Implement idempotency keys per charge; design state machine to handle all outcomes (first-only, both, second-only); mock PayGate timeout scenarios; integration test with artificial latency/failures | Dev/QA | Active |
| 5 | R05 | Rounding or remainder-cent logic assigns wrong amount to first or second card | Product | 3 | 3 | **9** | 🟠 HIGH | Decision table: test splits of 100, 101, 1000, 10001, 123456 cents; verify each cent is assigned exactly once and total equals original amount; automate in unit tests | QA/Dev | Active |
| 6 | R06 | UI allows invalid split amounts (negative, zero, exceeds total, non-integer) | Product | 3 | 3 | **9** | 🟠 HIGH | Equivalence partitioning: valid (1–total-1), boundary (0, 1, total, total+1), invalid (negative, decimal, string); input validation automation in UI + backend | Dev/QA | Active |
| 7 | R07 | PayGate integration error (wrong endpoint, missing fields, auth failure) on first or second charge | Product | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Integration test with PayGate mock covering: both charges succeed, first succeeds/second declines, both decline; verify request payload (amount, card, idempotency key); sandbox testing Tues/Thu for real PayGate | QA/Dev | Active |
| 8 | R08 | Payment data not persisted or reconciliation fails (charges recorded in DB but refund not logged) | Product | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Verify order record contains both charge IDs and refund ID; query DB to confirm state transitions; reconciliation query after each test scenario | QA/Dev | Active |
| 9 | R09 | Sensitive payment data (card tokens, amounts, refund status) logged or exposed in error messages | Product | 1 | 5 | **5** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Scan logs for PII; verify error messages do not expose card details or amounts; security code review of logging statements | Dev | Active |
| 10 | R10 | Performance degradation: split-payment flow adds latency to checkout (impacts 4,000/day throughput) | Product | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Baseline single-card checkout latency (e.g., 500ms); measure split-payment latency (should be ≤ 800ms, one extra API call); load test 50 concurrent split transactions | QA/Dev | Active |
| 11 | PR01 | PayGate sandbox unavailable or down during testing window (Tues/Thu only) | Project | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Proceed with mock-based testing Mon–Fri; batch sandbox tests into 2-hour windows on 10/29, 11/4, 11/6, 11/11; contact PayGate support if unexpected downtime; fallback: defer sandbox tests if unavailable | QA/Platform | Active |
| 12 | PR02 | Development not ready for testing by day 5; code merged with compilation errors or incomplete payGate mock | Project | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Daily standup tracking dev progress; code review before merge to release branch; PayGate mock acceptance criteria defined by day 2; escalate blockers immediately | Dev Lead | Active |
| 13 | PR03 | Defects found late (day 8–10) requiring rework; one QA tester @ 50% insufficient to re-test in time | Project | 3 | 3 | **9** | 🟠 HIGH | Release-gate approach: test critical paths early (day 4–5); prioritize defects by severity; devs fix in parallel with QA testing day 6–7; retest must complete by day 9 | QA/Dev Lead | Active |
| 14 | PR04 | Refund API endpoint not available or documented late; delays integration test design | Project | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Confirm refund API spec by end of day 1; mock it if not ready; design integration test cases day 2–3 independent of API availability; integration testing unblocked by day 4 | Payment Owner/Dev | Active |
| 15 | PR05 | Test data setup incomplete; PayGate mock does not support all scenarios (e.g., timeout, partial decline) | Project | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Fixture document by day 2: test accounts, card numbers, decline triggers; mock API behavior checklist (success, decline, timeout); validate with dev by day 3 | QA/Dev | Active |

### Risk Monitoring & Control
- **Weekly Review**: Every Friday, re-score active risks and note any changes in likelihood or impact
- **Escalation**: CRITICAL or HIGH risks escalated to PO if mitigation not on track
- **Control Action**: If a risk score increases or new defects indicate overlooked risk, update register with date and revised score
- **Completed Mitigation**: Mark risk as "Mitigated" when testing confirms defect not present; mark "Accepted" if risk accepted by PO despite testing

---

## 6. Test Approach

### 6.1 Test Levels and Distribution (Adaptive Pyramid)

This feature is **full-stack** (backend logic + frontend form + external API integration). Test distribution:

- **40% Unit Tests** (calculation, validation, state logic) → Developers + QA
- **40% Integration Tests** (PayGate mock, refund orchestration, data persistence) → QA + Developers  
- **20% E2E Tests** (full checkout flow in browser) → QA

### 6.2 Test Types and Techniques

| Test Type | Technique | Example Cases | Ownership |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
| **Functional** | Boundary Value Analysis, Equivalence Partitioning, Decision Tables | TC-001: Split 100¢ (50/50); TC-002: Split 101¢ (51/50); TC-005: Split 10000¢ (9999/1) | QA |
| **Calculation / Business Logic** | Equivalence + State Transition | TC-003: Remainder cent always to first card; TC-004: Both splits sum to original amount | Dev/QA |
| **Integration** | State Transition, Error Guessing | TC-006: First succeeds/second declines; TC-007: Both succeed; TC-008: Both decline; TC-009: Timeout on second charge | QA |
| **Refund Workflow** | State Transition + Timing | TC-010: Refund triggers within 2 seconds; TC-011: Refund triggers within 60 seconds; TC-012: Refund completes successfully | QA |
| **Validation / Input** | Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Values | TC-013: Negative amount rejected; TC-014: Zero rejected; TC-015: Amount > total rejected | QA |
| **Regression (Single-Card)** | Happy-Path Smoke Test | TC-016: Single-card payment succeeds (existing flow); TC-017: Single-card decline handled | QA |
| **Performance** | Load Testing (light) | TC-018: 50 concurrent split transactions complete in < 5 min; no timeout/error spike | QA |
| **Data Integrity** | Query Validation | TC-019: Order record contains both charge IDs; TC-020: Refund ID linked to declined charge | QA/DB |

### 6.3 Test Levels, Independence & Deliverables

| Level | Test Focus | Execution Environment | Independence | Deliverables |
|-------|-----------|----------------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Unit** | Amount calculation, input validation, state transitions | Dev local + CI pipeline | Dev (author+peer review) | Unit test suite in code repo; pass/fail per build |
| **Integration** | PayGate API calls (mock), charge/refund sequences, DB persistence | Staging with mock PayGate | QA (independent of dev) | Test cases (TC-006 to TC-012); test results with build hash + mock version |
| **System / E2E** | Full checkout flow (UI → backend → PayGate mock) | Staging + PayGate sandbox (Tues/Thu) | QA (high independence) | E2E test cases (TC-016 to TC-020); recorded results with screenshots/logs; sandbox results on real PayGate |
| **Regression** | Single-card payment (existing flow) | Staging | QA (high independence) | Smoke-test suite (TC-016, TC-017); pass/fail matrix |

### 6.4 Entry Criteria for System-Level Test Execution (When to START Testing)

- [ ] Feature code is fully implemented and merged to release branch
- [ ] Build succeeds with zero compilation/linting errors
- [ ] Staging environment is deployed and accessible
- [ ] PayGate mock API is available and documented (at least: success, decline, timeout responses)
- [ ] Test data fixtures are seeded (test accounts, card numbers, test orders)
- [ ] Single-card payment smoke tests pass (regression baseline)
- [ ] QA has write access to test results tracker and has received credentials for staging

### 6.5 Exit Criteria (When to STOP Testing & Release)

- [ ] Every release-gate case (TC-001 through TC-006, see § 6.7 below) executed and passing
- [ ] Zero open CRITICAL-severity defects; all CRITICAL defects resolved and re-tested
- [ ] Zero open HIGH-severity defects on the critical path (R01–R08), or each HIGH defect has a recorded PO exception + rollback plan
- [ ] Single-card regression smoke tests (TC-016, TC-017) pass 100%
- [ ] Refund automation verified on PayGate sandbox (Tues 11/11)
- [ ] Test results signed off by QA Lead and Product Owner (sign-off document in Jira)
- [ ] No new defects discovered on final sanity check (day 9 evening)

### 6.6 Release Gate: Smallest Viable Proof (5–8 Cases)

The release gate is the minimal set of cases that must pass to declare the feature ready. It answers: *Do the fixes work?* and *Did the change break anything that already worked?*

**Release Gate Test Cases:**

| TC ID | Title | What It Proves | Acceptance | Pass/Fail | Build | Env | Notes |
|-------|-------|----------------|-----------|-----------|-------|-----|-------|
| TC-001 | Split 100¢ evenly (50/50) into two cards; both succeed | Core split logic + both charges succeed | Both cards charged 50¢; total 100¢; order state is "paid" | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Happy path |
| TC-002 | Split 101¢ (51 first, 50 second); both succeed | Remainder-cent logic: extra cent goes to first card | First card 51¢, second 50¢; total 101¢; order state is "paid" | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Rounding rule validated |
| TC-003 | Split 1000¢ (700 first, 300 second); second card **declines**; refund triggers | Refund automation on second-charge decline | First charge reversed in < 60 sec; order state is "failed"; refund logged in DB | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Refund latency tracked |
| TC-004 | Invalid input: split amount = 0 or negative | Input validation rejects invalid splits | Error message displayed; no charges attempted; order remains "pending" | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Data integrity |
| TC-005 | Invalid input: split amount > total order amount | Input validation rejects overage | Error message displayed; no charges; order remains "pending" | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Boundary case |
| TC-006 | Single-card payment flow (existing) on same staging env | Regression: no regression in baseline payment flow | Card charged correct amount; order state is "paid"; same latency as pre-split baseline | ⬜ | [commit] | mock | Backward compat proof |

**Gate Verdict**: ✅ **RELEASE APPROVED** if all 6 cases pass + zero CRITICAL defects + PO sign-off. ❌ **HOLD RELEASE** if any gate case fails or CRITICAL defect remains open.

### 6.7 Test Data & Environment Requirements

**Test Data Fixtures (Seeded Before Testing):**

| Fixture ID | Description | State | Usage | Can Modify? |
|------------|-------------|-------|-------|------------|
| ORD-001 | Order: 100¢ total, no prior charges | "pending" | TC-001, TC-016 | Yes, reset after each test |
| ORD-002 | Order: 101¢ total, no prior charges | "pending" | TC-002, TC-003 | Yes, reset after each test |
| ORD-003 | Order: 10000¢ total, no prior charges | "pending" | Performance tests | Yes, reset after each test |
| CARD-VALID | Test card, always succeeds in mock | Valid in mock | All tests | No (read-only) |
| CARD-DECLINE | Test card, declines on second call in mock | Configured in mock | TC-003, TC-008 | No; config in mock API |
| CARD-TIMEOUT | Test card, times out after 5 sec in mock | Configured in mock | Timeout scenarios | No; config in mock API |

**Environment Configuration:**

| Environment | Purpose | PayGate Mock? | Real PayGate? | Access | Notes |
|-------------|---------|---------------|---------------|--------|-------|
| **Dev (Local)** | Unit test execution | N/A (mocked in code) | No | Developer machines | Fast feedback; no network calls |
| **Staging** | Integration & E2E tests (days 3–9) | Yes, configurable responses | No (most days) | QA + Devs; CI/CD pipeline | Mirrors prod schema; persistent test data |
| **Sandbox** | Real PayGate integration tests (Tues 10/29, 11/4, 11/6, 11/11) | No | Yes, PayGate sandbox | QA + Payment Owner | Limited windows; test cards provided by PayGate |

**Environment Sign-Off Checklist (Day 1–2):**
- [ ] Staging DB initialized with test fixtures
- [ ] PayGate mock API running and responding correctly (success, decline, timeout endpoints)
- [ ] PayGate sandbox credentials configured in staging deploy
- [ ] CI pipeline passing on release branch
- [ ] QA can execute test scripts and view logs
- [ ] Payment system logs are accessible (audit refund calls)

### 6.8 Metrics to Collect & Monitor

| Metric | Target | Collection | Reporting | Decision Gate |
|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| **Test Progress** | 100% gate cases executed by day 7; 100% analysis cases by day 9 | Case-by-case status in Jira | Daily standup + weekly chart | Hold release if < 100% gate by day 7 |
| **Defect Escape Rate** | < 1 defect per 1,000 cases executed (CRITICAL = 0) | Count failures re-tested and passed | Completion report | Release blocked if any CRITICAL remains |
| **Defect Closure Rate** | 100% CRITICAL/HIGH resolved by day 9 | Time from logged to closed | Triage dashboard | Escalate if HIGH open > 24h |
| **Regression Pass Rate** | 100% single-card smoke tests pass | TC-016, TC-017 results | Before release gate, after release gate | Do not release if < 100% |
| **Coverage** | 100% of 6 gate cases; ≥ 80% of analysis cases | Case execution tracker | Weekly | Adjust design scope if falling behind |
| **Refund Latency** | Mean < 10 sec, 100th percentile < 60 sec | Timestamp refund logged − timestamp decline recorded | Acceptance test results + sandbox run | Defect if any refund > 60 sec |
| **PayGate Mock Uptime** | 100% during testing days | Polling mock availability | Incident log | Escalate to dev if downtime > 30 min |

### 6.9 Deviations from Testing Policy

**Deviation 1: Sandbox-Only Testing Window**
- *Policy Expectation*: Full integration testing on real external APIs throughout the cycle.
- *Reality*: PayGate sandbox open only Tues/Thu (4 days out of 10); would delay release if sandbox were the only testing venue.
- *Deviation*: Mock-based testing days 3–9; real sandbox verification on final gate execution (day 7, sandbox open Tues 11/4) and release validation (day 10, sandbox open Tues 11/11).
- *Rationale*: Allows parallel testing while respecting PayGate's availability constraints; mock API closely mirrors real behavior (configured by Payment Owner); defects in mock-real Delta caught day 11–12 if needed.
- *Mitigation*: Sandbox test cases (TC-006 in gate) are mandatory; payment team on standby for sandbox issues.

**Deviation 2: Light Regression Testing**
- *Policy Expectation*: Full regression test suite for single-card payment to ensure no regressions.
- *Reality*: Single-card payment is high-volume (4,000/day); exhaustive regression would exceed 0.5 QA @ 50% time budget.
- *Deviation*: Smoke-level regression only: TC-016 (normal charge), TC-017 (decline). Existing unit tests (built by dev) cover edge cases.
- *Rationale*: Split-payment code path is isolated (new files/new conditional); risk of regression to single-card is Low (R03 score = 10, HIGH but mitigated by code isolation + prior unit test suite).
- *Mitigation*: Confirmation: devs certify code path isolation by code review day 2; existing single-card unit tests pass on release branch (CI gate).

---

## 7. Estimate (Effort & Resource Allocation)

### 7.1 Estimation Technique: Three-Point Estimation

**Formula**: E (Expected) = (a + 4m + b) / 6; SD (Standard Deviation) = (b − a) / 6

**Parameters:**
- **a (Optimistic)**: Code ready day 4, no major defects, all tests pass on first run → 2.5 FTE days
- **m (Most Likely)**: Code ready day 5, 1–2 defect cycles, sandbox validation on day 7–8 → 4 FTE days
- **b (Pessimistic)**: Code ready day 6, 3+ defect cycles, sandbox unavailable one day, defects in refund logic → 5 FTE days

**Calculation:**
- E = (2.5 + 4×4 + 5) / 6 = (2.5 + 16 + 5) / 6 = 23.5 / 6 ≈ **3.9 FTE days**
- SD = (5 − 2.5) / 6 = 2.5 / 6 ≈ **0.42 days**
- **Range: 3.5 to 4.3 FTE days (68% confidence)**

### 7.2 Translation to Calendar Time

- **1 QA tester @ 50% allocation** = 4 hours available per business day
- **3.9 FTE days** = 3.9 × 8 hrs = 31.2 hours QA labor
- **Allocated time: 10 working days × 4 hrs = 40 hours** → Sufficient with 8.8 hours buffer (22% margin)

**Breakdown by Activity:**

| Activity | Effort (FTE hrs) | Dates | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| Test design + case writing (days 1–2) | 6–8 | Wed 10/28 – Thu 10/29 | Parallel with dev setup; review requirements, PayGate mock spec |
| Environment setup + fixtures (days 1–3) | 2–3 | Wed 10/28 – Fri 10/30 | Validate staging, seed test data, mock API ready |
| Test execution on mock (days 4–7) | 12–14 | Mon 11/2 – Thu 11/6 | TC-001 to TC-015; defect logging; daily status |
| Defect triage + re-test (days 6–8) | 4–6 | Wed 11/5 – Fri 11/7 | 2x per-week triage; retest fixed defects |
| Sandbox verification (days 5 & 7) | 2–3 | Tues 11/4, Thu 11/6 | Real PayGate testing; sandbox windows only |
| Regression + gate final run (day 9–10) | 2–4 | Fri 11/7 – Tue 11/11 | TC-016, TC-017, gate retest; sign-off prep |
| **Contingency (buffer)** | **~8** | **As needed** | Defect rework, environment issues, schedule slip |
| **Total** | **~40 hours** | **10 working days** | @ 50% = 20 hrs/week available; 10 days = 40 hrs |

### 7.3 Assumptions Behind Estimate

1. **Code incremental delivery**: Split-payment code delivered in phases (days 3, 4, 5); QA starts testing day 4 on what's ready; no waiting for 100% completion.
2. **PayGate mock ready by day 2**: Developers provide mock API (or spec) by end of day 2; no delays integrating mock responses.
3. **Defect fix latency < 24h**: Developers fix reported defects same day or next morning; re-test not delayed by long fix cycles.
4. **Test case density**: ~20–25 test cases total (gate + analysis); ~30 min per case execution (dev/mock + validation); 15 min per case re-test after fix.
5. **No major PayGate sandbox downtime**: Sandbox available as scheduled (Tues/Thu); if unavailable, analysis cases delay but gate cases proceed on mock.
6. **Single tester competence**: QA tester is experienced in payment flows, PayGate, SQL, and Jira; no ramp-up time.
7. **No scope creep**: Feature scope locked; no new requirements during the 10-day cycle.

### 7.4 Resource Allocation

| Role | Time | Responsibility |
|------|------|-----------------|
| **QA Tester** | 50% (4 hrs/day for 10 days, 40 hrs total) | Test design, case execution, defect logging, progress reporting, release sign-off |
| **Dev 1** | 20% (2 hrs/day) | Build split-payment feature; provide/support PayGate mock; fix defects; code review of test findings |
| **Dev 2** | 20% (2 hrs/day) | Build refund automation; support integration tests; troubleshoot PayGate mock issues |
| **Dev Lead** | 10% (1 hr/day) | Defect triage, release readiness review, escalations |
| **Product Owner** | 5% (0.5 hrs/day) | Requirements clarification, gate approval, risk acceptance sign-offs |
| **Payment Systems Owner** | 5% (0.5 hrs/day) | PayGate integration advisory, sandbox credential management, incident response |
| **DevOps / Platform** | 5% (0.5 hrs/day) | Environment setup, test data seeding, incident response, credentials |

**Total Team Effort**: ~11.5 FTE days (0.5 tester × 10 + 0.2 dev × 10 × 2 + 0.1 lead × 10 + 0.05 × 10 × 4) ≈ **92 person-hours for the 10-day release cycle**

### 8.2 Resource Schedule (Gantt-Style)


# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope**: Release of split payment functionality enabling customers to pay a single order with two cards. Feature must integrate with external PayGate payment gateway and include automatic refund of the first charge if the second charge is declined. The existing single-card checkout must remain functional and unaffected.

**Objectives**:
- Verify split payment flow works correctly with two cards and accurate amount division
- Verify automatic refund logic triggers within 60 seconds when second charge is declined
- Verify remainder cent handling (odd amounts) places extra cent on first card
- Maintain zero regression on existing single-card checkout (4,000 orders/day volume)
- Confirm PayGate integration is stable and error handling is correct

**Test Basis**:
- Feature requirements: two-card split, amount division, remainder cent rule, 60-second refund SLA
- PayGate API documentation and sandbox contract
- Existing single-card checkout specification

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions**:
- Release date is 2026-11-11 (10 working days from today, 2026-10-28)
- PayGate sandbox environment will be available and stable every Tuesday and Thursday as scheduled
- Split payment feature code is fully implemented and integrated with PayGate API by Day 1
- Refund API endpoint is implemented and available for testing by Day 2 (2026-10-30)
- Test environment mirrors production PayGate integration configuration
- Single-card checkout code is stable with no concurrent changes during this release cycle
- The one tester has 20 hours per week available (100 hours total over the 10-day cycle)
- Developers can provide test data, fixture reset, and API troubleshooting on demand
- No dedicated QA environment or DevOps support exists; coordination is through the developer team

**Constraints**:
- PayGate sandbox available only Tuesdays and Thursdays (2 days per week)
- One tester at 50% capacity + two developers (limited human resources)
- Must not disrupt or block the existing 4,000 daily single-card orders
- 10 working days to release (tight timeline with sandbox blackout windows)

---

| 9 | P03 | Late discovery of PayGate API incompatibility or undocumented behavior; rework required | Project | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | Early API integration test (Day 2); API contract review with PayGate docs before Day 3; mock fallback for sandbox delays | Dev |
| 10 | P04 | Refund API not implemented or unstable by test start; blocks 50% of test scenarios | Project | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Refund API ready by Day 2, EOD (gate criteria); fallback: mock refund endpoint to proceed with design; track API stability in daily standup | Dev |
| 11 | R07 | PayGate sandbox unavailable or unstable on scheduled Tues/Thurs; cannot test against real API | Project | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Mock PayGate API with comprehensive error scenarios; run happy-path sandbox tests on both Tues & Thurs; fallback to staging if available | Dev / QA |
| 12 | R08 | Manual testing of concurrent multi-card payments misses race conditions or timing issues | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | State machine tests (automation); load test with concurrent orders (if capacity allows); focus manual on refund race scenarios | QA / Dev |
| 13 | R09 | Test data contamination or insufficient test card fixtures; unable to run repeat cycles | Project | 2 | 2 | 4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Document fixture set (test card numbers, states, reset procedures); use PayGate sandbox test cards only; restore fixtures between test cycles | QA / Dev |

---

## 6. Test Approach

**Test Levels & Distribution** (Payment processing feature—financial criticality):
- **Unit Tests (50%)**: Split logic, rounding, validation, refund calculation
- **Integration Tests (30%)**: PayGate API calls (mock + sandbox), refund endpoint, order state transitions
- **System/E2E Tests (20%)**: Full checkout flow, two-card flow, decline + refund, regression on single-card

**Test Types**:
- **Functional**: Amount split correctness, remainder cent rule, refund trigger, payment flow
- **Integration**: PayGate API contract compliance, error responses, refund API
- **Regression**: Single-card checkout; existing checkout flows; order history
- **Non-functional**: Refund SLA (60s timer), error message clarity, API timeout handling
- **Exploratory**: Edge cases, unusual card combinations, network degradation, user cancellation scenarios

**Test Techniques**:
- **Boundary Value Analysis**: Split amounts at boundaries ($0.01, $99.99, $100, $999.99), remainder cent cases
- **Equivalence Partitioning**: Small amounts ($1–$10), medium ($10–$100), large ($100–$999.99); split ratios (50/50, 30/70, 1/99)
- **Decision Tables**: First card success/decline × Second card success/decline → 4 scenarios (gate: 2 of 4)
- **State Transition**: Payment states (pending → charged → completed/refunded); refund state (pending → refunded/failed)
- **Error Guessing**: PayGate timeouts, invalid card, network errors, duplicate requests, race conditions

**Test Deliverables**:
- Test plan (this document)
- Test case suite (gate cases + P0/P1 cases, tracked in issue system)
- Fixture set document (test cards, reset procedures, fixture states)
- Regression suite baseline (single-card checkout critical paths)
- Daily progress reports (gate case status, blockers, defect summary)
- Completion report (all case results, coverage metrics, defect summary)

**Entry Criteria (When to START Testing)**:
- [ ] Split payment feature code merged to release branch, compiling with zero errors
- [ ] PayGate API integration implemented and code-reviewed
- [ ] Refund API endpoint implemented and accessible in test environment
- [ ] Test environment deployed and verified accessible
- [ ] PayGate sandbox credentials configured and sandbox connectivity confirmed
- [ ] Test card fixtures available and reset procedure documented
- [ ] Single-card checkout passing smoke test (sanity check for regression risk)

**Exit Criteria (When to STOP & RELEASE)**:
- [ ] All release gate cases (7 cases below) executed and passing on final build
- [ ] 100% of P0 test cases executed and passing (split flow, refund flow, remainder cent)
- [ ] 100% of P1 test cases executed or each failure has documented Product Owner exception
- [ ] Zero open 🔴 CRITICAL defects
- [ ] Zero open 🟠 HIGH defects (or documented PO exception)
- [ ] Single-card checkout regression suite passing (sample of 50+ daily orders)
- [ ] Final build deployed to staging; gate re-run passing on staging build
- [ ] Test summary report signed off by QA Lead and Product Owner

---

## 7. Release Gate

**Purpose**: Confirm split payment feature works correctly, refund logic is reliable, and single-card checkout regression is acceptable.

| Gate Case | ID | Purpose | Expected Result | Status | Build | Env |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | G01 | Even split, both cards succeed | Two charges processed, both amounts correct, order complete | ⬜ | — | — |
| 2 | G02 | Odd amount ($100.01), remainder on first card | First card: $60.01, Second card: $40.00, both succeed | ⬜ | — | — |
| 3 | G03 | Second card declined, auto-refund within 60s | First charge reversed; refund confirmed in PayGate within 60 seconds; order marked refunded | ⬜ | — | — |
| 4 | G04 | Single-card checkout still works ($100 charge) | Single-card flow executes without error; amount matches; no regression | ⬜ | — | — |
| 5 | G05 | Validation: cannot split to $0 on either card | Error message displays; order not charged; validation prevents invalid split | ⬜ | — | — |
| 6 | G06 | Large amount ($999.99) split correctly | Split calculated accurately; both charges succeed; amounts sum to total | ⬜ | — | — |
| 7 | G07 | Regression: sample daily volume (50 single-card orders) | All orders process without error; no latency regression vs. baseline | ⬜ | — | — |

**Test Execution Order**: Risk-based (gate cases in order 1→7; 🔴 CRITICAL risks first). Days 5–8 (sandbox available Tue 11/05 and Thu 11/07) prioritized for PayGate-dependent cases (G01–G03). Regression case (G07) runs last on final build to confirm no regressions on Day 9–10.

---

## 8. Estimate

**Estimation Technique**: Three-point estimation (expert-based)

**Breakdown**:
- Test planning, analysis, design: 8 hours
- Unit & integration test setup (mocks, fixtures): 12 hours
- Test execution (gate + P0 + P1 cases): 45 hours
- Sandbox-dependent testing (PayGate live API): 12 hours
- Regression suite execution: 8 hours
- Defect triage, retesting, sign-off: 10 hours

**Three-Point Estimate**:
- Optimistic (a): 60 hours (PayGate stable, no major defects, mocks reusable)
- Realistic (m): 83 hours (typical sandbox delays, 2–3 high defects requiring retest)
- Pessimistic (b): 110 hours (PayGate API incompatibility, refund logic rework, tight deadline pressure)

**E = (a + 4m + b) / 6 = (60 + 4(83) + 110) / 6 = 560 / 6 ≈ 93 hours**
**SD = (b − a) / 6 = (110 − 60) / 6 ≈ 8 hours**

**Estimate Range**: **85–101 hours (68% confidence interval)**

**Assumptions for Estimate**:
- Tester available 20 hours/week = ~100 hours total capacity over 10 days
- Developers available 4–6 hours/week for support (test data, API fixes, troubleshooting)
- PayGate sandbox available as scheduled (Tues & Thurs)
- Refund API stable by Day 2; no mid-cycle architectural changes
- Single-card checkout regression suite already exists (reuse, no build from scratch)
- No show-stopping defects requiring feature redesign

**Risk**: Estimate is at 93 hours with 100 hours capacity; margin of 7 hours. If sandbox becomes unavailable or refund API delayed, scope must be reduced to gate-only (≈40 hours core testing).

---

## 9. Budget and Schedule

**Timeline**:

| Phase | Days | Dates | Activities | Sandbox Status | Deliverable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Planning & Design | 1–2 | Wed 10/30, Thu 10/31 | Test plan, test cases, fixture design, PayGate API review | Available Thu 10/31 | Test case suite; fixture set document; sanity test on dev |
| Dev Integration & Mocks | 3–4 | Fri 11/01, Mon 11/04 | Unit test review, mock PayGate setup, integration tests, refund API contract verification | Unavailable | Integration tests passing on mocks; dev build confirmed |
| Sandbox Testing (1st cycle) | 5–6 | Tue 11/05, Wed 11/06 | Gate cases G01–G06 on sandbox; edge cases; error scenarios | Available Tue 11/05; unavailable Wed | Progress report: gate status, defects logged |
| Sandbox Testing (2nd cycle) & Regression | 7–8 | Thu 11/07, Fri 11/08 | Repeat gate cases (retest if defects fixed), regression suite, exploratory | Available Thu 11/07; unavailable Fri | Progress report: regression status, defect summary |
| Final Validation & Sign-Off | 9–10 | Mon 11/11, Tue 11/12 | Re-run gate on final build, PO walkthrough, defect review, sign-off | Unavailable (release day) | Completion report; gate pass/fail; sign-off by QA & PO |

**Resource Allocation**:
- **Tester (1 FTE @ 50%)**: 20 hrs/week; Days 1–10 allocated to this release (100 hours available vs. 93-hour estimate)
- **Developer 1 (2 FTE @ 25%)**: Feature implementation, PayGate integration, support testing
- **Developer 2 (2 FTE @ 25%)**: Refund API, test data setup, defect fixes
- **PO (on-call)**: Daily standup, defect triage, Day 10 sign-off

**Critical Path**:
1. Refund API ready by EOD Day 2 (2026-10-30) — blocks gate case G03
2. PayGate sandbox test on Day 5 (Tue 11/05) — only 1 of 2 sandbox days available before gate sign-off
3. Final build stable by EOD Day 9 (Mon 11/11) — gate re-run on Day 10

**Contingency**:
- If PayGate sandbox unavailable Day 5, defer to Day 7 (Thu 11/07) and compress regression to Day 9
- If refund API not ready Day 2, gate reduced to G01, G02, G04–G06 (defer G03 to Day 7)
- If defects found require >5 hours retest, exploratory cases deferred to post-release

---

## 10. Configuration Management of Testware

**Version Control & Identification**:
- Test cases tracked in [Jira/Azure ADO/GitHub Issues] with ID prefix TC-SPLIT-NNN
- Each test case links to feature requirement, risk register entry, and release notes
- Fixtures documented in dedicated fixture set file (e.g., `fixtures/split-payment-fixtures.md`); versioned with code

**Test Data & Fixture Management**:
- PayGate sandbox test cards listed in fixture set (card numbers, expiry, test scenarios they cover)
- Fixture states documented: e.g., "Test Card 4111-1111-1111-1111: Visa, always succeeds; reset required between cycles (no state retained)"
- Restore procedures: how to reset a contaminated fixture or recreate test data after a failed run
- Secure vault: PayGate sandbox credentials stored in env vars or secure vault; never in test scripts

**Test Environment Baseline**:
- Test environment version captured at sprint start: OS, database, PayGate sandbox configuration, build number
- Every test result records: build number, environment version, timestamp, tester name
- Example result row: `G01 | PASS | build-5.3.42 | test-staging-v2 | 2026-11-05 09:30 UTC | [Tester] | No defects`

**CI/CD Integration**:
- Unit & integration tests run on every PR merge (mocks, no sandbox)
- Gate cases re-run on release build before deployment (staging, with sandbox if available)
- Regression suite runs nightly on staging (single-card smoke tests)
- Results logged to test report and linked to release notes

**Traceability**:
- Traceability matrix: Requirement ↔ Test Case ↔ Defect ↔ Fix
- Every P0/P1 case linked to feature requirement ID (from product spec or user story)
- Every defect linked to failed case ID
- Every fix linked to defect ID and re-test case ID

**Rollback & Recovery**:
- If release fails gate, version of testware (cases, fixtures, results) archived with release tag
- Fixtures can be restored from backup or rebuilt per fixture set restore procedure
- Post-release: lessons learned logged and fixture set updated for next release

---

## 11. Test Monitoring, Control & Completion

**Metrics** (collected daily during Days 3–10):
1. **Test Progress**: Case count (total, designed, executed, passed, failed) vs. plan
2. **Defect Metrics**: Count by severity (🔴 CRITICAL, 🟠 HIGH, 🟡 MEDIUM, 🟢 LOW), status (open, fixed, re-tested)
3. **Coverage**: % of gate cases completed, % of P0 cases completed, % of regression executed
4. **Schedule Health**: Days remaining vs. % gate cases complete (target: 100% by Day 9 EOD)
5. **Risk Status**: Re-assess risk scores if new info surfaces (e.g., PayGate API slow on specific card type → increase R03 likelihood)

**Control Directives** (if monitoring flags a deviation):
- If gate case blocked by defect: bump defect to developer's Day 1 priority; set re-test date
- If sandbox unavailable >1 day: defer PayGate-dependent cases to next sandbox window; activate mock-only fallback
- If defect count > 5 on Day 6: extend Day 8 testing, defer exploratory, or escalate to PO for scope cut
- If tester capacity overrun (>85 hours by Day 7): reduce P1 scope or loop in developer to help execute regression

**Progress Report** (issued every 2–3 days):
- Brief status (1 sentence): "Gate 2/7 passing as of Thu 10/31; R02 (refund timing) blocked on API delay; on track."
- Blockers: e.g., "Refund API not yet integrated; unable to run G03 until resolved (targeted Wed 10/30 EOD)"
- Defect summary: open critical/high counts, resolution status
- Timeline risk: "Estimate 93 hrs vs. 100 hrs available; schedule OK if sandbox stable"

**Completion Report** (issued Day 10, after gate sign-off):
- Every case result (one row per case): ID | Title | Result (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED) | Build | Env | Notes
- Defect summary: All defects closed or with PO exception; severity distribution
- Coverage: % gate passing, % P0 passing, % P1 passing, regression status
- Metrics: Actual effort (tester hours logged), schedule variance, defect escape rates
- Lessons learned: What went well (e.g., "mock PayGate tests caught 2 edge cases early"), what didn't (e.g., "sandbox unavailable Day 5 compressed timeline")
- Sign-off: QA Lead approval, PO approval, date

**Post-Release Activities**:
- Archive test results and testware version with release tag
- Update fixture set with any new test card numbers or restore procedures learned
- Hold team retrospective (45 min): risks that materialized, estimate accuracy, process improvements
- Retire risks that were mitigated; carry forward risks that remain (e.g., PayGate sandbox availability) into next release cycle

---

## 12. Assumptions Summary

1. Split payment feature is fully implemented and compiling by start of test cycle.
2. Refund API is available and contract-documented by Day 2 (2026-10-30).
3. Single-card checkout code is stable with no concurrent changes.
4. Existing single-card regression test suite is available for reuse.
5. PayGate sandbox credentials and sandbox environment are configured and accessible.
6. One tester has 20 hours/week availability; two developers each have ~5 hours/week for QA support.
7. Test environment mirrors production PayGate integration without impacting live customer orders.
8. Defect severity classifications follow [Organization's] standard (CRITICAL = blocks release, HIGH = major feature impact, etc.).
9. Release decision made by Product Owner; QA can recommend but not unilaterally block release.
10. No additional regulatory (PCI-DSS, PSD2, etc.) compliance testing required beyond this scope; assumed covered by prior audits.

---

## 13. Deviations from Standard Test Policy

**N/A — No standard organization test policy cited.** This plan applies ISTQB CTFL v4.0 (Chapter 5) risk-based testing framework and follows payment industry best practices (financial transaction criticality, SLA enforcement, refund audit trail).

---

# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope**:
- New split-payment feature: customer selects split amount, two sequential charges via PayGate, automatic refund if second charge declines.
- Regression testing of single-card checkout (existing, ~4,000 orders/day).
- Integration with external PayGate API (sandbox only for testing).

**Out of Scope**:
- PayGate internal behavior and audit (boundary tested only).
- Refund UI or manual payment adjustment workflows.
- Load testing or performance optimization (not critical for single-payment-per-order model).

**Objectives**:
- Confirm split-payment logic calculates amounts correctly (including remainder-to-first-card rule).
- Confirm both charges execute and succeed when valid.
- Confirm automatic refund triggers within 60 seconds if second charge is declined.
- Confirm single-card checkout path is unaffected by split-payment code.
- Identify payment integrity defects before production release.

**Test Basis**:
- Feature specification (split amounts in cents, remainder rule, automatic refund).
- PayGate sandbox API documentation.
- Existing single-card checkout specification and regression suite.

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions**:
- Feature implementation will be code-complete and merged to release branch by end of day 4 (Nov 3).
- PayGate API is stable during available sandbox windows (Tuesdays and Thursdays).
- Automatic refund is implemented via PayGate refund API call (not a manual process).
- Remainder-cent logic (to first card) is implemented at payment service layer.
- Test card tokens (success, decline, timeout scenarios) are available in PayGate sandbox.
- Existing single-card regression suite is automated and passes on release branch baseline.
- QA can access staging and sandbox environments without delay.
- Developers are available for defect triage and clarification.
- Product Owner can sign off on gate results within 1 business day of completion.

**Constraints**:
- PayGate sandbox available **only on Tuesdays and Thursdays**; no testing Mon, Wed, Fri, weekends.
- One tester, half-time (4 hours/day, ~20 hours/week).
- **Release deadline: 10 working days** (November 11, 2026).
- No production downtime; existing checkout must operate continuously.
- No PCI-DSS re-audit scope (assumption: no new data storage changes).

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Owner | Responsibility | Relevance |
|------|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| Product Owner | (assumed) | Feature acceptance, gate approval | Defines feature requirements; approves release gate |
| Backend Developers (2x) | (dev team) | Implement split logic, refund state machine, API integration | Code ownership; defect resolution; design clarification |
| QA / Test Manager | (half-time tester) | Test planning, design, execution, reporting | Executes gate, regression, analysis; defect reporting |
| DevOps / Infra | (assumed) | Sandbox/staging access, environment stability | Provides test environment access; monitors availability |
| Payments Team Lead | (assumed) | Payment system oversight | Approves high-risk payment changes; authorizes production cutover |

---

## 4. Communication

- **Daily standup**: 10 min, verbally; blockers noted in Slack #payments-releases.
- **Defect reporting**: Ticket per defect (title, repro steps, expected vs. actual, severity, PayGate API version, build hash).
- **Gate status**: End of day Thursday (Nov 6): gate cases pass/fail, release recommendation (Go/No-Go).
- **Completion report**: Friday EOD (Nov 7): all cases executed, metrics summary, QA and PO sign-off.
- **Escalation**: If critical blocker, notify Payments Team Lead and dev lead immediately.

---

## 5. Risk Register

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|---|----|----|----------|---|---|-------|---------|--------------|-------|
| 1 | R01 | Remainder cent calculation error (off-by-one on split) | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Code review of split-logic function + boundary-value decision table tests (0, 1¢, max-1, max) | Dev/QA |
| 2 | R02 | Refund does not trigger when second charge declined | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Implement state-transition test matrix for all decline scenarios + automated E2E test; verify via PayGate API logs | QA/Dev |
| 3 | R03 | Refund takes >60 seconds to complete (timeout/latency issue) | Product | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Measure refund latency in sandbox (10+ iterations); set monitoring alert in staging; establish SLA verification gate case | QA |
| 4 | R04 | Single-card checkout broken by split-payment code changes | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Run full automated single-card regression suite before release gate; must pass 100% | QA |
| 5 | R05 | Race condition: both charges fail, refund still attempts (double refund) | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Test idempotent refund API (refund same transaction ID twice); verify only one refund appears in ledger | Dev/QA |
| 6 | R06 | PayGate timeout/transient error during second charge → unclear payment state | Product | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Test error cases (timeout, 5xx, rate-limit); verify customer sees clear error msg; verify first charge refunded if applicable | QA |
| 7 | R07 | First charge succeeds, second charge API call never sent (implementation bug) | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | Trace API calls in logs for each split transaction; verify both POST requests sent to PayGate | QA |
| 8 | P01 | PayGate sandbox unavailable outside Tues/Thurs; can't execute live tests on schedule | Project | 4 | 4 | 16 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Schedule test execution for Tues (Nov 3, 11, 18) and Thu (Nov 5, 7) only; move test-design and gap-review work to non-sandbox days; request PayGate support for extended sandbox access if slipping | QA/DevOps |
| 9 | P02 | Feature implementation incomplete by day 4 (code not merged to release branch) | Project | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Daily dev standup checkin; code review sign-off by EOD day 4; dev lead escalates if slipping by >4 hours | Dev Lead |
| 10 | P03 | Half-time tester cannot complete all cases within 10-day window | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Prioritize by risk (gate → CRITICAL → HIGH); automate single-card regression (already done); defer non-blocking exploratory edge cases to post-release if needed | QA |

**Risk Control Actions**:
- **R01, R02, R03, R04, R06, R07**: Mitigated by release gate (see Section 6).
- **R05**: Idempotency test designed into case set (Section 6).
- **P01**: Test schedule aligned to Tues/Thurs windows (Section 8); request PayGate support escalation if sandbox down.
- **P02**: Daily sync with dev team; if slipping, escalate to payments and dev leads by Nov 2 EOD.
- **P03**: Prioritize gate + regression; defer exploratory beyond gate to post-release patch cycle.

---

## 6. Test Approach

**Test Levels**:
- **Unit Testing** (Developer-owned): Split-logic calculation, state machine transitions. QA reviews test coverage, not re-tests.
- **Integration Testing** (QA-owned): Split + PayGate API, refund-trigger + PayGate refund API, error handling.
- **System/E2E Testing** (QA-owned): Full split-payment checkout flow, single-card regression, end-to-end via UI or API.
- **UAT** (Product Owner): Manual spot-check of happy path on staging.

**Test Types**:
- Functional: split amounts correct, both charges, refund on decline, remainder rule.
- Regression: single-card checkout unchanged.
- Integration: PayGate API (sandbox) integration, refund latency.
- Exploratory: error cases (network timeout, API errors, rate limits, card declines).
- Performance/Reliability: refund latency measurement (<60s confirmation).

**Test Techniques**:
- Boundary value analysis: split amounts ($0.00, $0.01, 50% even, 50% + remainder, max order total).
- Equivalence partitioning: decline on first vs. second charge, success on both.
- State-transition testing: charge states (pending, approved, declined, refunded, refund-failed).
- Decision table: split scenarios (even, uneven, zero first card, zero second card).
- Error guessing: PayGate timeout, 5xx error, rate limit, invalid card, network disconnect.

**Deliverables**:
- Release gate cases (5 cases, below).
- Functional test cases: split-payment scenarios (12 cases).
- Refund test cases: decline and recovery scenarios (8 cases).
- Regression suite: automated single-card tests (existing; run pre-gate).
- Defect log: each defect with title, repro, severity, status.
- Test execution log: per-case results, defect links, build version, date.
- Completion report: case summary, metrics, sign-off.

**Entry Criteria** (When to START Testing):
- [ ] Feature code complete, reviewed, and merged to release branch.
- [ ] PayGate sandbox endpoint accessible and verified from test environment.
- [ ] Test card tokens (success, decline, timeout) provisioned and confirmed in sandbox.
- [ ] Existing single-card test suite passing on release branch baseline.
- [ ] Feature specification and PayGate API docs available to QA.
- [ ] Staging environment deployed with split-payment code.

**Exit Criteria** (When to STOP Testing & Release):
- [ ] Every release gate case executed and passing.
- [ ] Single-card regression suite passing (100%).
- [ ] Zero open Critical-severity defects.
- [ ] Zero open High-severity defects (or documented Product Owner exception per defect).
- [ ] Refund latency confirmed <60 seconds on sandbox (min 3 test iterations).
- [ ] Test execution log and defect log complete and linked to all cases.
- [ ] Test summary signed off by QA Lead and Product Owner.

**Release Gate** (5 cases — minimal set covering changed and highest-risk behavior):

| ID | Case Title | What It Proves | Expected Result | Status | Notes |
|----|-----------|----------------|-----------------|--------|-------|
| **G01** | Split $100.00 evenly: $50.00 card 1, $50.00 card 2; both succeed | Both charges execute and succeed with correct split amounts | Two PayGate transactions: $50.00 and $50.00; both approved; ledger total = $100.00 | ☐ | Core feature happy path |
| **G02** | Split $100.01 with remainder: $50.00 card 1, $50.01 card 2 | Remainder cent (1¢) correctly goes to first card | Two charges: $50.01 (card 1) and $50.00 (card 2); both approved in PayGate | ☐ | Remainder rule verification |
| **G03** | First charge approved; second charge declined (insufficient funds) | Refund auto-triggers within 60s when second charge fails | First charge refunded in <60 sec; refund confirmed in PayGate audit log; no duplicate charges; customer sees single $0 net charge | ☐ | Critical: automatic refund SLA |
| **G04** | Single-card checkout: $100.00 on one card (regression check) | Regression: single-card path unaffected by split-payment code | Single transaction: $100.00; approved; no split logic triggered; checkout completes normally | ☐ | Regression gate |
| **G05** | Split $0.01 (minimum): $0.00 card 1, $0.01 card 2 | Edge case: zero amount on first card handled correctly | Card 1: $0.00 (charge skipped or $0 charge succeeds); card 2: $0.01; refund process handles zero-charge state | ☐ | Boundary condition |

**Test Independence**:
- QA tester is independent from development team (separate role, different person).
- Degree of independence: **Some** (QA from product team, but not external auditor). Rationale: payment feature is critical, but team is small and agile; external independent test would delay 10-day timeline.

**Test Data & Environment**:
- **Test environment**: Staging with split-payment feature code.
- **PayGate sandbox**: Card tokens for success scenario, decline (insufficient funds), decline (expired), timeout.
- **Fixture set**: See test-data/split-payment-fixtures.md (maintained in repo).
  - Test card tokens (no real PII stored; tokens provided by PayGate sandbox).
  - Expected outcomes per card type (success, decline, timeout).
  - Test order records with known user IDs for traceability.
- **Database state**: Orders seeded with test customer accounts; no shared state pollution; rollback after test cycle.

**Deviations from Standard Policy**:
- Unit test coverage (split-logic calculation) developed and owned by dev team; QA validates via integration/system tests, not isolated unit re-test (follows team's standard dev practice).
- Refund verification done via PayGate API audit logs and database state, not UI-only assertion (backend-driven feature).
- Load testing deferred (out of scope; single split per order is not high-volume concern within this release).
- No penetration testing (out of scope; handled by AppSec team in separate cycle).

**Metrics to Collect**:
- Test progress: % cases executed, % cases passed.
- Defect density: count by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low); defects per test case (target: ≤0.2 defects/case).
- Coverage: decision-table cases completed, boundary values tested, error paths covered.
- Risk mitigation: # CRITICAL risks mitigated (target: 2/2), # HIGH risks still open (target: 0).
- Project: actual hours spent vs. estimate (target: 19 ± 3 hours); days elapsed vs. 10-day window.
- PayGate availability: sandbox uptime during test windows (target: 100% Tues/Thurs).

---

## 7. Estimate

**Estimation Technique**: Three-point (expert-based PERT).

- **Optimistic (a)**: 12 hours
  - No implementation delays, sandbox available all scheduled days, zero defects on first run.
- **Most likely (m)**: 18 hours
  - One blocker day (sandbox down or code late 1 day), one defect found and re-tested, normal progress.
- **Pessimistic (b)**: 28 hours
  - Multiple sandbox outages, implementation slips 2+ days, 3+ defects requiring investigation and re-test.

**Expected Value (E)**:
$$E = \frac{a + 4m + b}{6} = \frac{12 + 4(18) + 28}{6} = \frac{112}{6} = 18.67 \text{ hours}$$

**Standard Deviation (SD)**:
$$SD = \frac{b - a}{6} = \frac{28 - 12}{6} = 2.67 \text{ hours}$$

**Final Estimate**: **19 ± 3 hours** (range: 16–22 hours)

**Confidence**: 68% (one standard deviation; 90% confidence = 19 ± 5.3 hours, range 13.7–24.3).

**Assumptions Behind Estimate**:
- Test case design (this plan) complete by EOD day 3 (Oct 31).
- Environment and PayGate sandbox access confirmed by EOD day 4 (Nov 3).

# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

### Scope

**In Scope:**
- New split payment feature: two-card checkout with customer-controlled split amount
- Cent-level amount splitting with remainder-to-first-card logic
- PayGate integration for both charges
- Automatic refund of first charge if second charge declines (60-second SLA)
- Regression testing of existing single-card checkout

**Out of Scope:**
- PayGate gateway infrastructure (assumed stable)
- Payment authorization rules or fraud detection (PayGate-owned)
- Multi-currency support (assumed single currency, or deferred to future release)
- Browser compatibility beyond Chrome/Firefox (assumed standard testing scope)

### Objectives

1. **Verification**: Split payment charges, split calculation, and refund automation work correctly
2. **Regression**: Existing single-card checkout remains functional; no breaks to 4,000 daily orders
3. **Risk mitigation**: Detect financial data loss, duplicate charges, failed refunds, and payment state inconsistencies before release
4. **Release gate**: Confirm changes are safe to deploy

### Test Basis

- Feature specification (split payment requirements)
- PayGate API documentation (charge and refund endpoints)
- Existing single-card checkout test cases
- Financial transaction integrity requirements

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

### Assumptions

- PayGate integration (charge and refund endpoints) is already implemented and stable
- Single-card checkout baseline is fully tested and working
- Test data (merchant account, test card numbers) is available in PayGate sandbox
- Environment deployments can be done on demand to staging; sandbox deployments depend on PayGate availability (Tues/Thurs only)
- 10 working days includes development, code review, and QA; actual QA window is 6–8 working days
- No partial refunds or multi-payment-method splits are in scope for this release
- Team has no blockers on development; feature is testable by day 8

### Constraints

- **PayGate sandbox availability**: Tuesday and Thursday only; limits hands-on testing to 4 days per 2-week cycle
- **Team capacity**: One tester at 50% (approximately 20 working hours per 10-day period), two developers for support
- **Release deadline**: 10 working days (hard constraint; testing ends when development must stop for release)
- **Environment dependency**: Staging can be used for dry runs, but PayGate integration requires sandbox or production-like test environment
- **Regression baseline**: 4,000 single-card orders per day in production; regression suite must be fast (<30 min) to fit daily run schedule

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Name / Team | Responsibility | Relevance to Testing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Product Owner | Product Team | Approve scope, accept risk and sign-off | Gate pass/fail decisions, risk acceptance on non-critical findings |
| QA Lead / Tester | QA (1 FTE × 50%) | Test planning, design, execution, defect reporting, gate sign-off | Owns all test activities, monitoring, and completion |
| Development Lead | Dev Team (2 FTE) | Implement feature, support test environment setup, fix defects | Provides code review support, environment stability, data for testing |
| Release Manager | Ops / Release | Coordinates deployment timing and rollback | Consumes gate pass/fail status; stops release if gate fails |

---

## 4. Communication

| Channel | Audience | Frequency | Content |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Daily standup | Dev + QA | 9:00 AM, 15 min | Blockers, environment status, test progress (% of gate cases run) |
| Test result sheet | Product Owner + Release Manager | Every execution run (typically end of day) | Gate cases status, new defects (ID, severity, blocker status) |
| Weekly progress report | Product Owner + Dev Lead | Friday EOD | Test coverage achieved, cumulative defect count, risk re-assessment, any gate delays or mitigation actions |
| Defect notifications | Dev + QA | As filed | Slack notification + linked ticket (P0/P1 defects within 1 hour; others by EOD) |

**Document templates:**
- Test result: one-line per case (ID, status, evidence/screenshot, defect link if failed)
- Defect ticket: title, severity, reproducible steps, PayGate response (if applicable), financial impact (if any)
- Weekly report: format in Configuration Management section (9) below

---

## 5. Risk Register (5×5 Matrix)

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | R01 | Refund fails or times out; first charge stays deducted after second charge declines | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Automated refund with timeout handler; state machine test covering decline + refund path; monitoring alert on refund failures post-release | QA + Dev | New |
| 2 | R02 | Duplicate charge: second charge succeeds but is recorded twice in payment records | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Idempotency key validation on PayGate; test for idempotent re-submit after network timeout; database row-level uniqueness constraint | Dev + QA | New |
| 3 | R03 | Split calculation error: remainder cent logic or rounding causes total ≠ order amount | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Decision table test (10+ split scenarios, edge amounts); edge-case-focused unit tests by dev team; automated regression check on every deploy | QA + Dev | New |
| 4 | R04 | Regression: existing single-card checkout breaks; customer orders fail | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Run single-card smoke suite before and after merge; 2 regression cases in gate; one end-to-end single-card case in daily regression run | QA | New |
| 5 | R05 | PayGate API integration: new split endpoint fails, times out, or returns unexpected error | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | PayGate integration test (mock + sandbox); error handling test (timeout, 4xx, 5xx responses); fallback behavior documented | Dev + QA | New |
| 6 | R06 | Payment data loss: charge succeeds but order record is not created or is corrupted | Product | 1 | 5 | 5 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Transaction boundary test (commit order record and PayGate charge atomically, or rollback both); database integrity check post-test | Dev + QA | New |
| 7 | R07 | Performance regression: split payment doubles checkout latency; impacts 4,000 daily orders | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Load test single-card + split-card under 4,000 req/day baseline; measure P95 latency; alert if split is >10% slower than single | Dev + QA | New |
| 8 | R08 | User experience: confusing split UI, validation errors not clear, money left on first card unintentionally | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Exploratory test of split UI flow; error message clarity check; 1 user acceptance case in gate | QA | New |
| 9 | R09 | PayGate sandbox unavailable beyond Tues/Thurs; test execution window blocked | Project | 3 | 3 | 9 | 🟠 HIGH | Use staging environment for dry runs and refund-decline scenario setup; execute core gate cases on Tues, retry Thu if needed; request emergency sandbox access if needed | QA + Ops | New |
| 10 | R10 | Timeline risk: 10-day release window + half-time tester not enough for full analysis; defects found post-release | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Prioritize risk-based gate cases (refund SLA, duplicate charge, rounding); run smoke regression daily; defer exploratory and edge-case analysis to post-release hotfix cycle if needed | QA + PO | New |
| 11 | R11 | Developers finish late; QA window compressed from 6 days to 2–3 days | Project | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Reserve Tues/Wed for testing; if code lands Friday, gate execution pushed to next Tues (slip release date or accept risk on PO approval) | PO + Release | New |
| 12 | R12 | Defect found in gate; retesting and fix deployment delays release by 1–2 days | Project | 2 | 2 | 4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Defect triage SLA: critical fixes within 4 hours; retest within 2 hours of fix; maintain 1-day buffer before final go-live decision | Dev + QA | New |

**Register Review Cadence**: Reviewed and re-scored at each weekly status report (Friday); escalated to PO if any score changes.

---

## 6. Test Approach

### 6.1 Test Levels, Types, and Techniques

| Level | Owner | Type | Technique | Coverage Target | Independence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unit** | Dev | Functional, boundary | Decision table (split calculation), equivalence classes (amount ranges) | 90%+ code paths in split logic, PayGate wrapper | None (author) |
| **Integration** | Dev + QA | Functional, error handling | State transition (charge → decline → refund); API mock testing (PayGate responses); database state validation | PayGate endpoint mocking, order record consistency, timeout handling | Some (peer review) |
| **System** | QA | Functional, regression, smoke | End-to-end scenario (split checkout flow), exploratory (UI edge cases), decision table (split amounts), single-card regression smoke | Full happy-path split flow, refund automation, single-card regression baseline | High (QA independent; no dev in room during test) |

### 6.2 Test Deliverables

1. Test cases (split payment feature, refund automation, edge cases)
2. Test data fixture set (seeded test cards, order fixtures)
3. Release gate results (signed-off by QA + PO)
4. Regression suite results (single-card smoke, daily runs)
5. Defect log (linked to tickets, severity tagged)
6. Test completion report (coverage achieved, findings, post-release monitoring plan)

### 6.3 Entry Criteria: When to START Testing

- [ ] Feature code is merged to release branch and compiled with no errors
- [ ] PayGate integration endpoints are implemented and reviewed
- [ ] Refund automation logic is code-reviewed
- [ ] Test environment (staging + sandbox access) is deployed and verified
- [ ] Single-card baseline regression suite passes in target environment
- [ ] Test data (seeded merchant account, test card numbers) is available in PayGate sandbox
- [ ] QA has reviewed feature spec and identified test cases

### 6.4 Release Gate (Go/No-Go Cases)

The gate comprises **7 cases** covering split logic, refund automation, and single-card regression. All must PASS to release.

| # | Case ID | What It Proves | Pass Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TC-501 | Split 50/50: order for $100, split $50/$50, both charges succeed | Both charges recorded; order total = $100; both card statements show correct amounts |
| 2 | TC-502 | Uneven split (remainder to first card): order $100.01, split $50/$50.01 | First charge = $50.01, second = $50.00; PayGate shows both successful; order amount = $100.01 |
| 3 | TC-503 | Refund SLA: second charge declines, first charge auto-refunds within 60 sec | First charge refunded within 60 sec; refund status in order record = "refunded"; customer does not see money deducted on statement |
| 4 | TC-504 | Edge case (small amount): order $1.00, split $0.50/$0.50 | Both charges succeed; order total = $1.00; no errors or data loss |
| 5 | TC-505 | Single-card regression: customer uses existing single-card checkout (not split) | Order placed and charged successfully; single-card checkout is unaffected by split code deploy |
| 6 | TC-506 | Single-card under load: simulate ~100 concurrent single-card orders | All orders charged successfully; no failures introduced; latency within baseline ±10% |
| 7 | TC-507 | PayGate error handling: second charge returns 5xx error; first charge must refund | First charge refunded within 60 sec; order marked as "failed"; customer is notified |

**Gate Execution Order (Risk-Based):**
1. TC-501, TC-502, TC-503 (critical refund and split logic; highest financial risk)
2. TC-504 (edge case, must not crash)
3. TC-505, TC-506 (regression; protects 4,000 daily orders)
4. TC-507 (error path; guards against data loss)

### 6.5 Full Analysis (Beyond Gate)

After gate passes, run exploratory and edge-case scenarios (time permitting):
- Split with full order amount on one card (e.g., $100 / $100 / $0) — should fail validation
- Negative amounts — should fail validation
- Non-integer cents in input (e.g., $10.123) — should fail validation
- Timeout during refund attempt; retry — should succeed on retry
- Customer cancels order during refund pending state — behavior documented

### 6.6 Independence of Testing

- **QA Tester (High Independence)**: Executes all system-level and gate cases independently; no dev involvement in test execution room
- **Dev Team (Some Independence)**: Reviews and tests integration layer with mock PayGate; peer-reviews unit tests but does not execute gate cases
- **Cross-review**: QA reviews dev unit/integration tests for coverage; dev reviews QA gate cases before execution

### 6.7 Metrics to Collect

| Metric | Purpose | Target | How Often |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Gate case pass rate | Go/no-go decision | 100% (all 7 pass) | Every run |
| Test case coverage (lines executed) | Functional completeness | ≥85% of split + refund code | End of execution |
| Defect density (defects / 1K lines of split code) | Quality benchmark | ≤1 critical, ≤2 high per 1K LOC | Weekly report |
| Regression suite pass rate | Baseline protection | 100% single-card cases | Daily run |
| Test execution progress (% of gate cases run) | Timeline tracking | 100% by day 8 | Daily standup |
| Refund SLA compliance (refunds ≤60 sec) | Critical path | 100% of refund cases | Every run |

### 6.8 Test Data and Environment Requirements

**Test Data Fixture Set:**

| Fixture | ID | Description | State | Resetability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Merchant Account | MER-001 | PayGate sandbox merchant (test API key) | Active; charges and refunds enabled | N/A (static; provided by PayGate) |
| Test Card - Approve | CARD-001 | Card number always approves charges | Not charged yet | Run reset script after each test block |
| Test Card - Decline 2nd | CARD-002 | Card that declines on 2nd charge in a session | Not charged yet | Run reset script; contact PayGate support if needed |
| Test Order - Base | ORD-001 | Order record for $100.00 | Draft (not charged) | Inserted via seeded data script; reset via `DELETE WHERE test_order_id = ORD-001` |

**Environment:**

| **Staging** | Dry-run split logic, UI, database state (no real PayGate calls) | Always | 80% of system tests (mock PayGate); refund SLA cannot be validated without real gateway |

| **Production** (post-release) | Monitoring; no testing | After release gate passes | Smoke monitoring, real-world defect detection |

### 6.9 Deviations from Standard Test Policy

- **No multi-environment regression**: Single-card regression runs only in staging (faster feedback); full regression on release day targets production-equivalent sandbox
- **Exploratory deferred to post-release**: Due to half-time capacity and 10-day timeline, exploratory testing (edge cases, usability) is documented as recommendations for a hotfix cycle if high-priority defects emerge
- **PayGate mock for dev, real calls for QA gate**: Dev team uses PayGate mock SDK for unit/integration tests to avoid sandbox availability constraints; QA uses real sandbox for gate execution to ensure PayGate integration is correct

---

## 7. Estimate

### Estimation Technique: Three-Point Estimation

Given constraints (half-time tester, 10-day window, PayGate sandbox availability), I use three-point estimation (CTFL v4.0 §5.1.4):

**Formula**: E = (a + 4m + b) / 6, where:
- **a** = optimistic (best case)
- **m** = most likely (realistic)
- **b** = pessimistic (worst case)

**Standard Deviation**: SD = (b − a) / 6

### Effort Breakdown

| Task | a (Optimistic) | m (Most Likely) | b (Pessimistic) | E (Estimate) | SD | Risk Factor | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Analysis & Design** | 3 hrs | 5 hrs | 8 hrs | 5.2 hrs | 0.8 | Low | Review spec, identify edge cases, design test cases |
| **Test Implementation** (write cases, set up data) | 8 hrs | 14 hrs | 20 hrs | 14 hrs | 2 | Medium | Includes test data fixture setup, PayGate sandbox configuration, automation of smoke regression |
| **Execution (Core Gate)** | 4 hrs | 6 hrs | 10 hrs | 6.3 hrs | 1 | **HIGH** (R09: sandbox availability) | Hands-on gate execution; 2 execution blocks (Tues + Thu); 1.5 hrs per run × 2 + retests |
| **Execution (Exploratory & Edge Cases)** | 2 hrs | 5 hrs | 10 hrs | 5.3 hrs | 1.3 | **HIGH** (Timeline risk R10) | Deferred if gate passes quickly; time-boxed to day 9 if buffer exists |
| **Defect Triage & Retesting** | 2 hrs | 4 hrs | 8 hrs | 4.3 hrs | 1 | Medium | Assumes 1–2 defects found in gate; retests after dev fixes |
| **Reporting & Completion** | 1 hr | 2 hrs | 4 hrs | 2.3 hrs | 0.5 | Low | Final test summary, sign-off, post-release monitoring plan |
| **TOTAL** | **20 hrs** | **36 hrs** | **60 hrs** | **37.4 hrs** | **6.7** | — | Half-time capacity = ~20–25 hrs available; estimate exceeds capacity |

### Estimate with Confidence Intervals

**Most Likely Scenario**: 36 hours (range: 29.7–42.3 hrs at ±1 SD)

**Available Capacity**: 
- 10 working days × 4 hours/day (50% FTE) = 40 hours
- Less daily standups, blockers (~2 hrs) = ~38 productive hours
- **Shortfall risk**: ~1–2 hours if anything slips

### Critical Path & Assumptions

1. **PayGate sandbox windows (Tues/Thu)** limit execution to 4 days in 10; gate execution must fit into one 6-hour window on Tues, with Thu reserved for retests
2. **Dev finishes feature by day 6** to allow 4 days of QA; if slips to day 8, timeline becomes critical
3. **No P0 defects in gate** (1-2 retests assume P1/P2 defects only)
4. **Single-card regression suite runs in <20 min** to fit daily smoke
5. **Exploratory testing is deferrable** if gate takes longer than expected

### Recommendations for Timeline Mitigation

- **Parallel testing**: Staging environment dry-runs (day 5–6) overlap dev coding, reducing gate execution to ~4 hours
- **Prioritize gate**, defer exploratory to post-release analysis phase if needed
- **Pre-execution**: Prepare test data and merchant account setup on day 3–4 (before gate day)

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

### Identification and Version Control

All testware is version-controlled in the project repository under `qa/split-payment-5.3/`:

```
qa/split-payment-5.3/
├── test-cases.md          (v1.0; versioned by date and author)
├── test-data-fixtures.sql (v1.0; seeded data, reset script)
├── test-results.md        (v1.0; filled in during execution)
├── risk-register.md       (v1.0; updated weekly)
└── completion-report.md   (v1.0; filled at end of testing)
```

### References by Identifier and Version

- **Test Case ID Format**: `TC-5XX` (split payment feature, v5.3). Each case includes test data fixture ID (e.g., ORD-001) and PayGate sandbox merchant ID (MER-001)
- **Defect ID Format**: `DEF-SSSSS` (issue tracker auto-generated); linked in test result and risk register
- **Build Version**: Every result includes build number (e.g., `split-payment-v5.3-build-042`) and environment (staging / PayGate sandbox / production)
- **Test Result Traceability**: Each row in `test-results.md` includes `[TC-XXX] | [Build] | [Env] | [Status] | [Evidence]`

### Baselined Environments

| Environment | Baseline Version | How Established | Restoration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### Restorable Baselines

- **Before each gate execution**: Run `qa/split-payment-5.3/test-data-fixtures.sql` to reset test order records and merchant account state in PayGate sandbox
- **After each execution run**: Snapshot test results in `test-results.md` with timestamp and build number; archive to `qa/split-payment-5.3/results-archive/` with date prefix
