# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

### Scope
- **In Scope**: Split payment feature allowing customers to pay for one order with two cards; amount splitting logic in cents (remainder cent on first card); automatic refund of first charge if second charge declines within 60 seconds; regression testing of existing single-card checkout.
- **Out of Scope**: PayGate internal transaction processing, fraud detection, multi-currency conversion, mobile app (test web only).

### Objectives
1. Verify split payment amount splitting is mathematically correct in all scenarios
2. Confirm both card charges succeed in happy path
3. Validate automatic refund executes within 60-second SLA when second charge declines
4. Confirm existing single-card checkout remains fully functional
5. Identify defects before release to production

### Test Basis
- Feature specification (split payment logic with cent handling)
- PayGate API documentation for dual-charge and refund operations
- Existing checkout regression requirements

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

| # | Assumption / Constraint | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Testing Environment | Staging environment with PayGate sandbox available; test data includes valid/invalid card tokens |
| A2 | Build Readiness | Feature merged to dev branch; deployment pipeline available Tue/Thu only (PayGate sandbox constraint) |
| A3 | External Dependency | PayGate sandbox is the single source of truth; all production-like charge testing depends on Tue/Thu availability |
| A4 | Refund Monitoring | Refund status is queryable from order management system; automated refund events are logged and timestamped |
| A5 | Regression Scope | Single-card checkout covers ~4,000 daily orders; test represents 95th percentile of order amounts and card types currently used |
| A6 | Test Data | Fixture cards available for success and decline scenarios; test data can be reset between test runs |
| A7 | Release Readiness | 10 working days available; no competing urgent production issues; QA half-time equals 40 hours/week |

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Name / Team | Responsibility | Independence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Product Owner** | Payments Team | Define acceptance criteria, review release gate, sign off exit criteria | N/A |
| **Developer (2)** | Backend/Payment Services | Implement feature, support environment setup | N/A |
| **QA / Test Manager** | 1 person, 0.5 FTE | Test planning, execution, defect reporting, release gate validation | Some — same team as developers; external review of gate results by PO |
| **DevOps** | Platform Team | Environment deployment, sandbox access scheduling | N/A |

**Independence Rationale**: QA is co-located with dev team (some independence); test results reviewed externally by Product Owner before release gate sign-off (increases confidence).

---

## 4. Communication

| Form | Frequency | Audience | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily Standup | Daily | Devs, QA, PO | Test progress, blockers (esp. sandbox availability) |
| Test Status Report | Wed & Fri | PO, Devs | % of test cases executed, pass/fail counts, critical findings |
| Release Gate Review | Day 9 | PO, QA Lead | Gate case results, go/no-go recommendation, known issues |
| Defect Ticket | As found | Dev team | One ticket per unique defect, linked to test case ID and build version |

---

## 5. Risk Register (Product & Project Risks)

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|---|---|---|----|---|---|----|----|-----|---|
| 1 | R01 | Refund not triggered within 60-second SLA when second charge declines | Product | 5 | 5 | **25** | 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Unit test refund timeout logic; integration test with PayGate sandbox; automated E2E with declining card; add 60-sec timer assertion; code review by 2 devs | Dev/QA |
| 2 | R02 | Amount split calculation incorrect (off-by-one or rounding error) | Product | 4 | 5 | **20** | 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Unit test all split scenarios (even, odd, $0.01, large amounts); decision table for remainder handling; code inspection | Dev/QA |
| 3 | R03 | First charge succeeds but second fails and first is not reversed | Product | 4 | 5 | **20** | 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Refund integration test; end-to-end failure path; database state verification; rollback logic code review | Dev/QA |
| 4 | R04 | Existing single-card checkout broken by split payment changes | Product | 3 | 5 | **15** | 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Regression suite on 20 existing checkout scenarios; daily regression runs; automated E2E for happy path and edge cases | QA |
| 5 | R05 | PayGate API integration fails (timeout, invalid credentials, rate limits) | Product | 3 | 4 | **12** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Mock PayGate in unit/integration tests; live sandbox testing on Tue/Thu window; fallback error handling; timeout configuration reviewed | Dev |
| 6 | R06 | Data inconsistency (order/transaction records not synchronized after split charge) | Product | 3 | 4 | **12** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Database transaction tests; state verification after each charge; audit log inspection; integration test with DB rollback scenarios | Dev/QA |
| 7 | R07 | Insufficient testing time due to PayGate sandbox availability (Tue/Thu only) | Project | 4 | 3 | **12** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Schedule integration/E2E tests for Tue/Thu windows only; run all unit/mock tests on other days; parallel unit test execution; prioritize gate cases on first available sandbox day | QA |
| 8 | R08 | Defect found late (post-gate) and cannot be fixed before release | Project | 2 | 5 | **10** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Risk-based test prioritization (CRITICAL cases first); daily gate execution; feature flag to disable split payment if blocker found | PO/Dev |
| 9 | R09 | Edge case: amounts that don't split evenly across cards (e.g., $0.01, $0.02) | Product | 3 | 3 | **9** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Boundary value analysis; test $0.01, $0.02, odd amounts; verify remainder always on first card; decision table test | QA |
| 10 | R10 | QA resource unavailable (0.5 FTE constraint; other priorities) | Project | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 **HIGH** | Devs write unit tests; automate regression suite; QA focuses on integration/E2E; daily sync on resource conflicts | QA/PO |
| 11 | R11 | PayGate sandbox down on critical test day (Tue/Thu) | Project | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 **MEDIUM** | Pre-test sandbox health check; fallback to mocked PayGate for design/dry runs; defer live testing to next available day | DevOps |
| 12 | R12 | Refund latency monitoring unavailable or inaccurate | Product | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 **MEDIUM** | Add explicit timestamp logging for refund initiation; query refund status via API; manual verification in first release; add monitoring dashboard | Dev |

---

## 6. Test Approach

### 6.1 Test Levels, Types & Techniques

#### Test Pyramid Distribution (Full-Stack Payment Feature)
- **50% Unit Tests** (40 cases): Amount splitting logic, refund timer, validation
- **30% Integration Tests** (24 cases): PayGate API mocking & sandbox, database transactions, order state
- **20% E2E Tests** (16 cases): Full checkout flow, payment success/decline scenarios, regression

#### Test Types per Risk Level

| Risk Level | Test Techniques | Coverage Target | Test Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 CRITICAL (R01–R04) | Decision table, boundary value analysis, state transition, equivalence partitioning | 100% of paths | Unit + Integration + E2E |
| 🟠 HIGH (R05–R10) | Boundary value, error guessing, exploratory | ~80% of paths | Integration + E2E |
| 🟡 MEDIUM (R11–R12) | Happy path, basic exploratory | ~50% of paths | E2E or manual |

#### Detailed Test Design

**Unit Tests (Amount Splitting & Refund Logic):**
- Test split calculation: even amounts, odd amounts, $0.01, large amounts ($10k+)
- Test remainder assignment: always goes to first card
- Test refund timeout: 60-second boundary, just-under and just-over scenarios
- Test validation: negative amounts, zero amounts, amounts exceeding order total
- Test error handling: invalid card tokens, missing payment method

**Integration Tests (PayGate API & Database):**
- Charge first card: success, decline, timeout, invalid credentials
- Charge second card: success, decline (triggers refund), timeout
- Refund execution: triggered on second decline, within 60 seconds, successful and failed refund scenarios
- Order state transitions: pending → both charged → complete, or pending → first charged → refunding → refunded
- Database consistency: order record, transaction log, refund audit trail all in sync

**E2E Tests (Checkout Flow):**
- Happy path: customer selects split, enters amounts, both charges succeed, order confirmed
- Second card decline: both charges shown in order history, refund visible within 60 seconds
- Edge case: $0.01 total (1 cent on first card, 0 on second)
- Existing single-card checkout: unchanged flow, still works
- Error recovery: retry second charge, abandon and retry entire order

### 6.2 Test Deliverables
1. Test Plan (this document)
2. Test Case Repository: 80 cases (40 unit, 24 integration, 16 E2E) with IDs, preconditions, steps, expected results
3. Test Data Fixture Document: Card tokens (valid & decline), order amounts, test customer accounts
4. Risk Register (Section 5, updated at milestones)
5. Release Gate Results: 6-case table (Section 9)
6. Test Execution Summary: Pass/fail counts, defect log, coverage report
7. Completion Report: Lessons learned, testware handover

### 6.3 Entry Criteria for System Test Execution
- [ ] Split payment feature code merged to `dev` branch, reviewed and approved
- [ ] PayGate sandbox sandbox is confirmed available (scheduled for Tue 2026-11-05 or Thu 2026-11-07)
- [ ] Staging environment deployed with feature code; payment endpoints accessible
- [ ] Test data fixture prepared: 5 valid cards, 3 decline cards, test customer accounts
- [ ] Test case repository finalized and reviewed by dev team
- [ ] Regression test baseline (single-card checkout) passing on staging

### 6.4 Exit Criteria (Release Gate)
- [ ] All 6 release gate cases (Section 9) executed and passing
- [ ] 100% of P0 test cases executed; zero P0 failures or all have PO exception
- [ ] 100% of P1 test cases executed; zero P1 failures or all have PO exception (max 2 exceptions)
- [ ] Zero open Critical-severity defects
- [ ] Zero open High-severity defects (exceptions require PO + Legal sign-off for payment features)
- [ ] Single-card checkout regression suite passes (20 core cases)
- [ ] Test summary and defect log signed off by QA and PO
- [ ] Build version and environment version documented in results

### 6.5 Deviation from Standard Policy
- **PayGate Sandbox Constraint**: Live integration testing is limited to Tue/Thu windows (R07 mitigation). Unit and mock-based integration tests run daily; live sandbox tests batch-scheduled for sandbox availability. This is acceptable because unit + mocked integration covers 90% of risk; live tests verify integration only.
- **Limited QA Resource**: Developers write unit tests; QA focuses on integration and E2E. Daily standups sync priorities. This is acceptable because unit test responsibility is shared with authors.
- **Tight Timeline**: Test case design begins immediately; execution in parallel with late-stage dev work (integration test stable on Day 5+). Regression cases run on Day 8 to verify no regressions before gate.

### 6.6 Metrics to Collect
1. **Test Progress**: % of cases designed, % executed, % passed (tracked daily)
2. **Defect Metrics**: Count by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low), age, status (open/closed), linked to risk IDs
3. **Coverage**: % of code branches covered by unit tests, % of PayGate API paths covered by integration tests
4. **Risk Metrics**: Risk scores tracked from register; risks closed by test passing
5. **Time Metrics**: Actual vs. planned for design, execution, defect investigation
6. **Regression Baseline**: % of single-card checkout cases still passing

### 6.7 Test Data & Environment Requirements

**Test Data (Fixture Set):**
- **Valid Card 1**: Token `tok_valid_001`, limit $10,000, expected behavior: charge succeeds
- **Valid Card 2**: Token `tok_valid_002`, limit $10,000, expected behavior: charge succeeds
- **Decline Card 1**: Token `tok_decline_001`, expected: declined on second charge only (for R01 testing)
- **Decline Card 2**: Token `tok_decline_002`, expected: declined immediately (for fallback testing)
- **Test Customer 1**: `cust_test_001`, no order history, used for E2E clean-slate tests
- **Test Customer 2**: `cust_test_002`, existing single-card order history, used for regression
- **Test Order Template**: $100.00 order, breakable into $60 + $40, $50 + $50, $1 + $99, etc.

**Environment:**
- Staging server with split payment code deployed
- PayGate sandbox credentials configured (provided by DevOps)
- Test database with fixture data pre-seeded
- Refund status queryable via admin API or order detail page
- Logs aggregated and timestamped (for 60-second SLA verification)

### 6.8 Independence of Testing
**Test Design**: Conducted by QA (some independence from dev; devs provide API specs).
**Unit Test Execution**: Developers write and run; QA spot-checks coverage.
**Integration & E2E Test Execution**: QA executes (high independence from dev on results interpretation).
**Release Gate Review**: QA + external PO review (very high independence for go/no-go decision).

---

## 7. Estimate

### Estimation Technique: Expert-Based (Three-Point Estimation)

Decomposition by activity:

| Activity | Low (a) | Most Likely (m) | High (b) | PERT Estimate E = (a+4m+b)/6 | SD = (b-a)/6 | Assumptions |

| Integration test development (24 cases, mocked) | 8h | 12h | 16h | **12.3h** | 1.3h | PayGate API is well-documented |
| Integration test execution (live sandbox, Tue/Thu) | 6h | 10h | 14h | **10.0h** | 1.3h | Sandbox availability risk (R07) included |

### Available Capacity
- QA: 1 person at 0.5 FTE = 20 hours/week × 2 weeks = 40 hours
- Developer unit test time (from dev budget): ~20 hours across 2 devs
- **Total available**: ~60 hours (QA) + shared dev bandwidth

### Adjustment for Constraints
- **Sandbox availability (Tue/Thu only)**: Live integration testing compressed into Tue/Thu windows; plan **parallel work**: unit tests on Mon/Wed/Fri, live integration on Tue/Thu. Deferred live testing to Day 5 (Thu 2026-11-05) at earliest.
- **Tight timeline (10 working days)**: Test design & case development must complete by Day 5 (Thu 2026-11-01) to allow 5 days of execution. **Critical path**: design → unit → mock-integration → live integration → E2E → regression → gate.

### Risk-Adjusted Effort
- R01, R02, R03, R04 (CRITICAL): Allocate extra effort to unit & integration testing
  - Add +5 hours to integration test execution (deeper scenarios)
  - Add +2 hours to E2E (more failure path coverage)

**Revised Estimate: 84–94 hours**, assuming:
- Dev team provides 20+ hours for unit tests
- QA gets uninterrupted 40 hours/week (no competing tickets)
- No sandbox outages beyond 1 day (fallback to mocked testing)
- Defects are not complex show-stoppers (avg 1 hour to investigate per defect)

**Gap**: Estimate exceeds QA availability by ~24–54 hours. **Mitigation**: Scope reduction (E2E cases reduced to 12 instead of 16) or prioritization (CRITICAL/HIGH cases only; MEDIUM cases deferred to hotfix if time runs out).

---

## 8. Budget and Schedule

### Timeline (10 Working Days, 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-10)

| Phase | Days | Dates | Milestones | Resource |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Planning & Design** | 1–2 | Oct 28–29 (Mon–Tue) | Test cases finalized, entered into tracking | QA, Devs |
| **Unit & Mock Integration** | 3–5 | Oct 30–Nov 3 (Wed–Sun → Mon) | 40 unit + 24 mocked integration cases passing | Devs + QA |

### Critical Path
```
Design (2d) → Unit (3d) → Mock Integration (1d) → 
Live Sandbox (Tue Nov 5) → E2E (2d) → Regression (2d) → Gate (1d)
```
**Float**: Minimal; any delay in design ripples to execution. **Mitigation**: Parallelize unit & mock-integration on days 3–5; pre-design gate cases by day 1 to enable early smoke test.

### Budget
- **QA Labor**: 1 person × 0.5 FTE × 2 weeks × $rate/hour (assume $75/h junior QA, $120/h senior) = ~$3k–$4.8k
- **Dev Labor (unit tests)**: 2 people × 20 hours shared = 40 person-hours (included in dev budget)
- **Tools**: Existing test automation tools (no new licenses); PayGate sandbox (no cost)

---

## 9. Release Gate

The release gate is the smallest set of test cases that must pass to answer: **(1) Does the split payment feature work? (2) Did we break the existing single-card checkout?**

| Gate Case ID | Scenario | What It Proves | Expected Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G-001** | Split payment: $100 split $60/$40, both cards valid | Amounts split correctly; both charges succeed | Two transactions created: $60 and $40; order total $100; order status = complete | ⬜ Pending |
| **G-002** | Split payment: $99 split $50/$49, both cards valid | Remainder cent goes to first card (math: $50 + $49 = $99) | Two charges: $50 (first) + $49 (second); order complete | ⬜ Pending |
| **G-003** | Split payment: First charge $60, second charge declines | Refund triggered on second decline; automatic refund within 60 seconds | First charge ($60) reversed (refund issued); refund timestamp ≤ 60 sec from decline; order status = refunded | ⬜ Pending |
| **G-004** | Single-card checkout: $100 on one card (existing flow) | Regression: single-card checkout still works | One transaction $100 created; order status = complete (same as pre-split-feature) | ⬜ Pending |
| **G-005** | Split payment: $0.01 total split, first card $0.01, second card $0 | Edge case: very small amounts handled | First charge $0.01; second charge $0 or skipped; order complete | ⬜ Pending |
| **G-006** | Split payment: Second charge declines, refund fails (PayGate error) | Error handling: refund failure logged and visible to customer | First charge $X reversed attempt made; error logged; customer notification sent; order status = refund_pending_retry | ⬜ Pending |

### Test Execution Order (Release Gate)
1. **G-001, G-002, G-004** (Day 9, morning): Happy path cases; no dependencies; if any fail, gate fails immediately.
2. **G-003** (Day 9, midday): Refund path; depends on Day 6 live sandbox test of PayGate decline scenario; if fails, investigate timeout logic.
3. **G-005** (Day 9, afternoon): Edge case; low risk but exercises boundary condition; skippable if time is critical (not a blocker).
4. **G-006** (Day 9, late): Error path; depends on ability to simulate PayGate refund failure; if not reproducible, mark as "Out of scope — PayGate behavior" and accept as known issue.

**Rationale**: Risk-based order (CRITICAL cases first). Happy path gates the release; refund case gates the refund feature specifically. Edge and error cases are included because they are in scope but lower priority if time runs out (documented as scope reduction).

---

## 10. Configuration Management of Testware

### Identification & Version Control
- **Test Plan**: `test-plan-split-payment-5.3.md`, version 1.0 (in repo `/docs/qa/plans/`)
- **Test Cases**: Spreadsheet `split-payment-test-cases.xlsx`, tab-separated or GitHub issue tracker with labels `split-payment` and `release-5.3`

### Baseline & Version
Every test result must record:
- **Build Version**: Git commit SHA or build ID (e.g., `build-20261105-1430`)
- **Environment Version**: Staging deploy timestamp and configuration (e.g., `staging-2026-11-05T14:30Z, PayGate sandbox v2.1`)

### Traceability & References
- Test cases linked to feature spec (requirement IDs or user story IDs)
- Test cases linked to risk register (risk ID from Section 5)
- Defect tickets linked to test case ID that found them (e.g., defect `PAY-512 found in case T-045`)
- Gate results linked to release tag (e.g., release v5.3, tag `v5.3-rc1`)

### Repository & Restorable Baseline
- Test code (unit, integration, E2E automation) lives in `/tests/` directory of payment service repo
- Test data fixtures stored in `/tests/fixtures/split-payment/` as JSON or SQL seed scripts
- Results archived in `/test-results/split-payment-5.3/` with timestamp subdirs (one per test run)
- Baseline single-card checkout test cases live in `/tests/regression/checkout/` and are not modified by split-payment work
- Restore procedure: `git checkout [commit-sha]` for code; re-seed fixtures from scripts; re-run regression suite to verify baseline

### CI/CD Integration
- Unit tests run on every commit to `feature/split-payment` branch (GitHub Actions or CircleCI)
- Mock integration tests run daily on `dev` branch
- Live sandbox integration tests scheduled only on Tue/Thu (cron: `0 10 * * 2,4`, i.e., 10 AM Tue/Thu)
- Regression suite runs before any merge to `main` (pre-merge gate)
- Test results captured and linked to build artifacts

---

## 11. Monitoring, Control & Reporting

### Metrics Collected Daily
| Metric | Target | Collection Method | Corrective Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| % Test Cases Executed | 10% by Day 2, 50% by Day 5, 100% by Day 9 | Manual count in tracker | Accelerate design or defer low-priority cases |
| % Test Cases Passed | 95%+ | Automated result reporting | Investigate failure; assign to dev; retest after fix |
| Defect Count (Open) | 0 Critical, ≤1 High, ≤3 Medium | Defect tracker | Stop and fix Critical; document High for PO decision; MEDIUM into backlog post-release |

### Monitoring Frequency & Governance
- **Daily Standup** (10 min): QA reports test cases executed yesterday, blockers (esp. sandbox), plan for today
- **Wed & Fri Status Reports** (email): Test progress %, defect counts by severity, risks re-scored
- **Day 5 & Day 9 Gates** (meeting, 30 min): Formal review of progress against exit criteria; decision to proceed or escalate

### Corrective Actions (Examples per CTFL v4.0 §5.3)
1. **Defect: Refund not triggered within 60 sec** (found Day 6) → **Directive**: Stop E2E testing; dev team investigates and fixes refund timer logic; QA retests by EOD Day 7; if fix confirmed, resume E2E.
2. **Sandbox down on Tue (Day 6)** → **Directive**: Shift live integration tests to Thu (Day 8); complete mock-integration tests first to unblock E2E design.
3. **Regression suite finds 3 broken single-card cases** → **Directive**: Rollback split-payment code; dev team investigates integration point; QA re-runs regression to confirm fix; do not proceed to gate until regression passes.

# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope**: Addition of two-card split-payment capability to the existing single-card checkout flow. Customers select a primary card amount; the remainder goes to a secondary card. Both charges route through PayGate. Automatic refund of the primary charge if the secondary charge is declined within 60 seconds.

**Test Basis**: Feature specification (split payment feature brief); existing single-card checkout specification; PayGate API documentation; PCI-DSS and payment processing compliance requirements.

**Objectives**:
- Verify split-payment calculation logic (cent remainder handling) is correct.
- Confirm both charges execute through PayGate as intended.
- Validate automatic refund mechanism completes within 60-second SLA.
- Ensure zero regression in existing single-card checkout (4,000 orders/day volume must remain stable).
- Identify integration issues with PayGate sandbox before production release.

**Test Levels**: Unit, Integration, System (E2E), Regression.

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

| Assumption | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Checkout system is API-driven (REST/GraphQL backend, web frontend) | Standard modern e-commerce architecture. Informs test pyramid and automation approach. |
| Single-card checkout exists as stable, tested baseline | Stated in feature brief; used to scope regression suite. |
| PayGate sandbox mirrors production behavior | Required for confidence in release candidate; test against sandbox only due to availability window. |
| "Release date: 10 working days" means go-live, all testing complete by 2026-11-11 | Starting from 2026-10-28; excludes weekends and typical org holidays (none assumed in this 2-week window). |
| Test environment is independent of production; orders do not leak to live systems | Standard practice; no test-to-production pollution. |
| Existing single-card regression suite is runnable and maintainable | If not, effort estimate adjusts upward; plan assumes it exists. |
| Developer availability: 2 developers can contribute 20–30% effort to test automation | Release-critical feature; devs expected to help scaffold and maintain test infrastructure. |
| Refund latency is measurable in test (timestamps logged; PayGate refund state queryable) | Required to verify 60-second SLA; absence of this raises a HIGH-risk project issue. |
| Browser support: Chrome, Firefox, Safari (or whatever current checkout supports) | No new browser matrix for this feature; use existing single-card scope. |

**Constraints**:
- **PayGate sandbox available Tuesdays and Thursdays only**: Integration and E2E test windows are 2 days/week; impacts scheduling and test-execution order (see Section 8, Schedule).
- **One tester, half time (~20 hrs/week effective)**: Limits manual exploratory and regression scope; automation and developer support are mandatory.
- **10 working days to release**: ~40 effective hours from the tester; devs must automate the majority of suite.
- **Regression on 4,000 daily orders**: Failure in single-card flow is high-visibility; regression suite must be small, fast, and high-confidence.

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Name | Responsibility | Test Relevance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Product Owner** | Not named; assumed assigned | Feature approval, definition, acceptance | Sign-off on release gate pass/fail; exception authority for P1+ failures |
| **Dev Lead** | Not named; one of two developers | Feature implementation, code review | Code walkthrough for test design; test-automation pairing |
| **QA Lead / Test Manager** | This plan's author | Test planning, scheduling, monitoring, sign-off | Owns plan execution, daily standups, risk mitigation, completion report |
| **Test Engineer** | One tester, half time | Test analysis, design, execution, defect reporting | Executes manual E2E and exploratory tests; co-authors automation with devs |
| **DevOps / Deployment** | Not named; assumed assigned | Environment setup, PayGate sandbox access, build promotion | Ensures test and staging environments mirror prod config; gates production release |
| **Compliance / Legal** | Not named; assumed assigned | PCI-DSS audit trail, payment regulations | Non-functional tests (audit logging, data handling) may be in scope; confirm with stakeholder |

**Independence Degree**: Test Engineer is independent (not a developer on the feature) → **Some independence**. Rationale: One dedicated tester reduces author-bias in single-card regression; developers assist automation to meet timeline, maintaining separation of concerns.

---

## 4. Communication

| Cadence | Form | Audience | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Daily** (async) | Slack message or stand-up 15 min | Dev lead, test engineer, devops | Blockers, PayGate sandbox availability status, test-execution progress, defect count |
| **Every execution cycle** (Tues/Thurs) | Test execution log + screenshot evidence | QA lead, product owner | Cases run, pass/fail count, gateway response times, any manual findings |
| **Weekly** (Wed or Fri) | Progress report: test metrics, risk register review, schedule confidence | Product owner, dev lead, QA lead | Test coverage %, defect severity distribution, timeline risk (stay green/yellow/red), forecast for gate pass |
| **At release** | Test completion report + sign-off | Product owner, DevOps, Compliance | All cases logged with results, test summary (coverage, defect closure), gate sign-off, deployment readiness |

**Document Templates**: Use existing org templates if available; else store all case results (ID, name, steps, result, evidence) in a shared sheet or test-management tool (e.g., ADO/JIRA/TestRail); version control for non-live artifacts (test scripts, fixtures).

---

## 5. Risk Register (5×5 Matrix)

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | R01 | Split amount calculation is incorrect (e.g., off-by-one on cent remainder, rounding errors, total != original amount) | Product | 4 | 5 | **20** | 🔴 CRITICAL | Unit test decision table for boundary splits (0¢, 1¢, 50¢, 99¢ remainder); automated regression on 20+ split amounts. Dev code review. | Dev + QA |
| 2 | R02 | Secondary charge is declined; primary charge is NOT refunded, or refund is delayed >60s, leaving customer charged and angry | Product | 3 | 5 | **15** | 🔴 CRITICAL | E2E test: force secondary decline, verify refund in PayGate within 60s; mock PayGate delays to verify SLA under stress; log timestamps; set up monitoring alert on refund lag. | Dev + QA |
| 3 | R03 | Both charges execute, but first charge is refunded even when second charge succeeds (logic inverted or race condition) | Product | 3 | 5 | **15** | 🔴 CRITICAL | E2E happy path (both succeed) + exploratory async-order testing; state transition test (charge 1 → charge 2 → no refund); code review of refund trigger logic. | Dev + QA |
| 4 | R04 | Existing single-card checkout is broken by split-payment code (e.g., shared payment path, regression in middleware) | Product | 3 | 5 | **15** | 🔴 CRITICAL | Regression suite: 8 single-card cases (happy path, card decline, timeout, 3DS, etc.) run on every build; smoke test before release gate. | QA |
| 5 | R05 | PayGate sandbox is unavailable outside Tue/Thu, delaying integration testing and blocking release candidate validation | Project | 4 | 4 | **16** | 🔴 CRITICAL | Schedule all integration & E2E execution on Tue/Thu only (see Section 8); pre-stage test data and mock PayGate responses for unit & design phases; dev local mocks for offline design. Escalate to DevOps if sandbox down on scheduled day. | DevOps + QA |
| 6 | R06 | Test harness or automation framework is not ready; half-time tester cannot execute full suite manually in time | Project | 3 | 4 | **12** | 🟠 HIGH | Dev 1 owns test automation scaffold (API client, assertion library, retry logic); test engineer pairs for case scripting. Automated cases prioritized: split calculation, refund SLA, regression. Exploratory scripted locally by Wed. Resume point documented daily. | Dev + QA |
| 7 | R07 | Defect discovered late (day 8–9) in refund logic; refactor and re-test takes >2 days, missing release window | Product | 2 | 5 | **10** | 🟠 HIGH | Refund logic tested first, in parallel with split-calculation unit tests (risk-based execution order). Early E2E smoke on day 3. Code review by Dev 2 before integration testing. | Dev + QA |
| 8 | R08 | Split-payment feature leaks sensitive card data (PAN, CVV) in logs, audit trail, or error messages, violating PCI-DSS | Product | 2 | 5 | **10** | 🟠 HIGH | Security code review by Dev 2 (card data handling); log analysis test (grep for unmasked PAN/CVV); automated check in CI. Compliance sign-off before release. | Dev + Compliance |
| 9 | R09 | Concurrent orders or race conditions: two split payments on same card at same second; one succeeds, one hangs or double-charges | Product | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Load/concurrency E2E test (10 concurrent split orders); state transition test; PayGate idempotency key handling verified in code review. | Dev + QA |
| 10 | R10 | PayGate API response times slow down under test volume; SLA monitoring is not instrumented, so refund delay is not caught | Product | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | E2E test records timestamps; refund SLA assertion built into case logic (automated fail if >60s). Devops instruments PayGate call latency in staging logs. | Dev + QA + DevOps |
| 11 | R11 | Tester is unavailable mid-week (illness, vacation); no backup, manual testing stalls | Project | 2 | 4 | **8** | 🟠 HIGH | Prioritize automated cases; document resume points daily by EOD Thu. If tester unavailable, defer non-critical exploratory tests (R12, R13) to post-release. | QA |
| 12 | R12 | Edge cases not explored: $0.01 split, negative amount attempted, invalid card combinations, concurrent decline+timeout | Product | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Exploratory testing session (2–3 hrs, test engineer) after gate cases pass; log findings as tickets, not gate-blockers. Scripted positive cases before release. | QA |
| 13 | R13 | Documentation for split-payment checkout UX is missing or unclear; customers confused, support load spikes | Product | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | UX acceptance test (does UI clearly show the two amounts?); user journey walkthrough with PO. Post-release support plan in place. | PO + QA |
| 14 | R14 | Staging environment PayGate credentials are wrong or expired; cannot test integration | Project | 2 | 3 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Verify PayGate creds & sandbox access by EOD Thu of week 1. Store securely (no repo); alert DevOps if timeout occurs. | DevOps |
| 15 | R15 | Single-card regression suite is flaky; false fails waste tester time and delay release gate sign-off | Project | 3 | 2 | **6** | 🟡 MEDIUM | Smoke single-card suite on each build; isolate & fix flaky cases before feature testing starts (day 1 activity). | Dev + QA |

**Risk Monitoring**: Review register on Friday of each week and after any major defect discovery. Re-score if facts change (e.g., PayGate sandbox outage confirmed for a specific day = L increases; test automation delivered early = Project risks drop). Mark date of any re-score.

---

## 6. Test Approach

### 6a. Test Levels & Types

| Test Level | Responsibility | Independence | Scope | Technique | Deliverable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Unit** | Developer (Dev 1) | None (author) | Split-amount calculation logic; refund-trigger condition; input validation | Boundary-value analysis (split amounts: 0¢, 1¢, 50¢, 99¢ remainder, $0.01–$9999.99); decision table (both charges succeed, only 2nd declines, both decline, timeout, network error) | `test_split_payment.py` or equivalent; ≥20 cases; ≥90% branch coverage |
| **Integration** | Dev 2 + Test Engineer | High (independent test engineer validates) | Split payment API endpoint → PayGate sandbox; both charge calls; refund trigger; response parsing | API contract test (PayGate request/response shape); happy path (both succeed); secondary decline → refund; timeout & retry logic | `test_split_payment_api.py`; ≥8 cases; all PayGate paths exercised |
| **System (E2E)** | Test Engineer + Dev 1 | High (test engineer scripts; dev assists automation) | End-to-end checkout flow: select two cards, enter split amount, submit, both charges on PayGate, order state transitions, refund if needed | Happy path (order placed, both charged, order confirmed); secondary decline (primary refunded, order cancelled); single-card path still works; concurrent orders (stress) | Playwright or Selenium; ≥12 cases; includes regression on single-card flow |
| **Regression** | Test Engineer (manual smoke, automated runs) | High | Existing single-card checkout; no split involved | Happy path (card accepted, order placed); card declined; timeout; 3DS/2FA (if in original scope) | Automated regression suite; ≥8 cases; run on every build + release gate; <5 min duration |

### 6b. Test Pyramid (Architecture-Based)

**Diagnostic Question**: "Where does the business logic live?" → Payment processing is API-driven (backend); split-calculation and refund-timing logic is backend; checkout UI is frontend. **Preset: Full-stack web app (React + API)** → 40% Unit · 40% Integration · 20% E2E.

**Distribution** (25 total cases):
- **Unit (10 cases, 40%)**: Split-calculation boundary, decision-table, input validation.
- **Integration (10 cases, 40%)**: PayGate API contract, both-charge paths, refund logic, error responses.
- **E2E (5 cases, 20%)**: Happy path, secondary decline, concurrent, UI validation, UX clarity.

*Note*: Regression (8 single-card cases) runs separately; scored as defensive, not part of feature pyramid. Release gate pulls 5–6 top cases across levels.

### 6c. Testing Quadrants Alignment

| Quadrant | Coverage | Technique | Automation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Q1 (Technology-facing, Supports Team)** | Unit tests (split calc, refund logic); API contract tests (PayGate shape) | Boundary-value, decision table | ✅ Automated (CI) |
| **Q2 (Business-facing, Supports Team)** | Acceptance: "When I split $50.00 as $30 + $20, both charges succeed and I see split confirmation" | Happy-path scenario, UX walkthrough with PO | ✅ Automated (E2E) + Manual (PO walkthrough) |
| **Q3 (Business-facing, Critiques Product)** | Exploratory: edge cases (tiny splits, card limits, declined scenarios), UX confusion, support issues | Exploratory, user-journey testing | 🟡 Manual (post-gate, if time) |
| **Q4 (Technology-facing, Critiques Product)** | Non-functional: latency (refund SLA <60s), security (PAN/CVV not logged), concurrency (10 simultaneous orders) | Load test, security code review, log inspection | ✅ Automated (E2E load, CI security scan) |

### 6d. Entry & Exit Criteria

**Entry Criteria for System-Level Test Execution** (When to START Testing):
- [ ] Split-payment feature is implemented, code merged to `release/5.3` branch, zero linting/build errors.
- [ ] PayGate sandbox credentials loaded to staging environment; connectivity confirmed (test API call succeeds).
- [ ] Unit test suite passes (≥90% coverage on split calculation and refund logic).
- [ ] Test environment (staging) is deployed, orders do not leak to production.
- [ ] Existing single-card regression suite is confirmed runnable (smoke run passes <5 min).
- [ ] Test data: 10+ test cards in PayGate sandbox (mix of success/decline scenarios).

**Exit Criteria for Release** (When to STOP Testing & Release):
- [ ] All **Release Gate cases** (see below) passed and signed off by QA Lead and Product Owner.
- [ ] 100% of P0 cases (split calculation, refund SLA) executed and passing.
- [ ] 100% of P1 cases (both-charge paths, secondary decline, single-card regression) executed and passing, or PO-approved exceptions logged.
- [ ] Zero open **Critical** defects; zero open **High** defects (or PO exception with signed risk acceptance).
- [ ] Single-card smoke regression (8 cases) passes on latest build.
- [ ] Security code review completed; no unmasked card data in logs.
- [ ] Test completion report signed by QA Lead and Product Owner.
- [ ] **Gate sign-off blocks production release if not achieved.**

### 6e. Release Gate (5–6 Minimum Cases)

The release gate is the smallest set that answers "Does the fix work? Did we break anything?". Built from high-risk cases: split-calculation correctness, refund SLA, secondary-decline flow, single-card regression.

| Gate ID | Case Name | What It Proves | Priority | Automation | Expected Result | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G01** | Split $50.00 into $30.00 + $20.00 (even split) | Correct calculation, both charges succeed, order confirms | P0 | ✅ Automated E2E | Both PayGate charges logged; order state = `confirmed`; customer sees split confirmation | — |
| **G02** | Split $50.01 into $30.00 + $20.01 (remainder on first) | Remainder-cent logic correct; first card charged $30.01, second $20.00 | P0 | ✅ Automated Unit + E2E | First charge = $30.01, second = $20.00; total = $50.01; order confirmed | — |
| **G03** | Secondary card declined; primary refunded within 60s | Automatic refund SLA met; order cancelled; customer not double-charged | P0 | ✅ Automated E2E (mock decline, measure refund latency) | Primary charge refunded (PayGate refund log shows <60s delta); order state = `cancelled`; no error to customer | — |
| **G04** | Single-card checkout (existing flow) still works: charge $50.00, one card, order confirms | Zero regression on 4,000 daily orders | P1 | ✅ Automated Regression | Existing flow unchanged; order confirms with one charge; <100ms latency delta from baseline | — |
| **G05** | Both charges declined; order is not placed | Handles double-decline gracefully; no partial charge | P1 | ✅ Automated E2E (mock both declined) | Order creation fails; no charges logged in PayGate; customer sees error message; rollback clean | — |
| **G06** | Concurrent split orders (5 simultaneous): each order charges correctly on both cards, no cross-contamination | No race conditions or card mixing under load | P1 | ✅ Automated E2E (load test) | All 5 orders complete independently; each has correct two charges; no double-charges or dropped payments | — |

**Gate Execution Order** (Risk-Based):
1. **G01 & G02** (calculation correctness) — day 2 or 3 (unit tests run first; E2E smoke as soon as integration ready).
2. **G03** (refund SLA, highest-risk product impact) — day 4 (depends on refund logic unit test passing).
3. **G04** (regression, protects daily revenue) — day 5 (runs on every build; final smoke before gate).
4. **G05 & G06** (error handling, load) — day 6–7 (exploratory paths; defects here are P1 but not gate-blockers if dev fixes available).

**Override of execution order**: PayGate sandbox available only Tue/Thu → all integration & E2E execution pushed to those days; unit tests run any day.

### 6f. Test Data & Environment

**Test Data Fixture Set**:

| Fixture ID | Card Description | Test Purpose | State | Read/Write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **F01** | Visa 4111111111111111 (test success card) | Happy path: both charges succeed | Valid, no holds | Read-only (use per test; do not persist state) |
| **F02** | Visa 4000000000000002 (test decline card) | Secondary decline: force second charge to fail | Valid, auto-declines on transaction | Read-only |
| **F03** | Visa 5555555555554444 (Mastercard test) | Cross-brand validation | Valid, success | Read-only |
| **F04** | Amex 378282246310005 (test success) | 3-card type coverage | Valid, success | Read-only |

*Preconditions*: All cards are PayGate sandbox-only; zero real charges. Test-environment order state is isolated (does not affect production). Refund state queryable from PayGate sandbox API within 5s.

**Environment Requirements**:
- **Staging**: Checkout app, payment-processing service, database (test orders isolated by namespace or TTL).
- **PayGate Sandbox**: Credentials pre-loaded; accessible Tue/Thu only; refund polling available (<5s latency to see refund status).
- **Local Dev**: Mock PayGate responses for offline unit-test development; Docker Compose or equivalent.

### 6g. Non-Functional Test Focus

| Non-Functional Attribute | Technique | Threshold | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Performance (Refund SLA)** | E2E test with clock measurement; PayGate API latency logging | Refund initiated <60s after decline detection | QA + Dev |
| **Concurrency** | 10 simultaneous split orders; state isolation check | Zero cross-order charge contamination; all 10 complete within 30s | QA |
| **Security (PAN/CVV masking)** | Log file grep + code review | No unmasked card numbers in logs; test assertions | Dev + Compliance |
| **Backward compatibility** | Single-card regression suite | <100ms latency delta from baseline; same pass rate (>99%) | QA |

### 6h. Deviations from Standard Test Policy

**Deviation 1**: Integration testing is **compressed to Tue/Thu only** due to PayGate sandbox availability window. Mitigation: Unit tests and local mocks run daily; integration is scheduled, not ad hoc.

**Deviation 2**: **Exploratory testing is post-gate** (not pre-release) due to half-time tester and 10-day timeline. Rationale: Gate covers critical paths; exploratory findings logged as tickets, not release blockers. Post-release optional if timeline allows.

**Deviation 3**: **Code review substitutes for some integration testing** (refund-trigger logic, card-data masking). Rationale: Critical financial logic requires architectural review; testing alone cannot catch design flaws. Dev 2 assigned to code-review paired with test cases.

---

## 7. Effort Estimate

**Estimation Technique**: Expert-based (Wideband Delphi, three-point).

**Decomposition**:

| Task | Dev 1 (hrs) | Dev 2 (hrs) | Test Eng (hrs) | Total (hrs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Test Planning & Analysis** | — | — | 3 | 3 |
| **Unit Test Suite (split calc, refund logic)** | 8 | — | 2 (review) | 10 |
| **Integration Test Suite (PayGate mocking, API)** | 6 | 2 (code review) | 3 | 11 |
| **E2E Test Automation (Playwright, happy + sad paths)** | 4 | — | 6 | 10 |
| **Regression Suite (single-card smoke, automated)** | 2 | — | 3 | 5 |
| **Manual Exploratory Testing** | — | — | 4 | 4 |
| **Defect Triage & Re-test** | 2 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| **Security & Compliance Review** | — | 3 (code review, PAN/CVV masking) | 1 | 4 |
| **Test Execution & Monitoring** | — | — | 8 | 8 |
| **Documentation & Completion Report** | — | — | 2 | 2 |
| **Contingency (10% buffer)** | 2.4 | 0.7 | 3.6 | 6.7 |
| **TOTAL** | **24.4** | **7.7** | **39.6** | **71.7 hrs** |

**Three-Point Estimate (optimistic / most-likely / pessimistic)**:
- **Optimistic (a)**: 60 hrs (no defects, zero PayGate integration surprises, automation scaffold exists).
- **Most Likely (m)**: 72 hrs (1–2 defects found & fixed, 1 automation spike, normal surprises).
- **Pessimistic (b)**: 90 hrs (3+ defects requiring refactor, PayGate sandbox outage delays testing, test-harness rebuild).
- **Expected (E)**: E = (60 + 4×72 + 90) / 6 = **73.33 hrs**.
- **Standard Deviation**: SD = (90 − 60) / 6 = **5 hrs**.

**Range**: 68–78 hrs at 68% confidence; 63–83 hrs at 95% confidence.

**Assumptions**:
- Test automation scaffold (API client, assertion helpers, retry logic) is available by day 1 or can be scaffolded in <4 hrs by Dev 1.
- Single-card regression suite is runnable and maintainable (not broken; <2 hrs to fix if flaky).
- PayGate sandbox is up Tue & Thu; no outage >2 hrs (or test is rescheduled).
- No scope creep: split payment only; single-card checkout is in-scope for regression, not refactored.

**Resource Allocation**:
- **Dev 1**: ~24 hrs / 80 hrs in release cycle = **30% of dev capacity** (implementation is ~50 hrs; test automation is ~24 hrs).
- **Dev 2**: ~8 hrs / 80 hrs = **10% of dev capacity** (code review, security, support).
- **Test Engineer**: ~40 hrs / 40 hrs = **100% of half-time role** (per constraints).

**Feasibility Check**: 71.7 hrs fits in 10 working days (40 + 40 dev-hours from two devs + 40 half-time tester = 120 total capacity). Schedule is tight but achievable if PayGate sandbox is available and no major bugs emerge.

| **Integration Test Cases** | `git` repo (`tests/integration/test_split_payment_api.py`) | Git commit SHAs; tagged at integration-ready | Baseline = all cases passing on Tue/Thu sandbox day | ✅ Run on Tue/Thu only (scheduled CI job); gate on all pass before release | Yes; git history |
| **E2E Test Cases** | `git` repo (`tests/e2e/split_payment.spec.js` or `.ts`, Playwright) | Git commit SHAs | Baseline = gate cases (G01–G06) passing on latest build | ✅ Run nightly on staging; gate cases run Tue/Thu on sandbox | Yes; git history |
| **Regression Suite** | `git` repo (`tests/regression/single_card.spec.js`) | Git commit SHAs; version locked to baseline single-card build | Baseline = 100% pass on current prod-equivalent environment | ✅ Smoke run on every build; full run before release | Yes; git + environment snapshot |
| **Test Data Fixtures** | Test-data generator script (`scripts/seed_test_data.sh`) or inline (PayGate sandbox cards are well-known) | Git; fixtures are static (no sensitivity data stored) | Initial seed on day 1; re-seeded if corrupted | ✅ CI: confirm fixture availability before test run | Yes; script is reproducible; PayGate sandbox resets nightly |

| **Completion Report** | Wiki or shared doc; archive copy in git (`docs/release-5.3-completion.md`) | Dated; filed after release; archived | Final report is sign-off; locked after release | N/A | Yes; archived version-tagged |

**Versioning Strategy**: All test code (`*.py`, `*.js`, `*.sh`) is in git on `release/5.3` branch. Configuration (PayGate creds, environment URLs) is in a **secrets manager** (not git). Build artifacts (test results, screenshots) are logged with build number and timestamp; retained 90 days or per org retention policy.

**Baselined Environments**: Staging and PayGate sandbox each have a known-good baseline snapshot (git commit + environment config version). If an environment is corrupted, restore from baseline snapshot and re-run test suite.

**CI/CD Integration**:
- **Unit tests**: Run on every commit; block merge if coverage <90%.
- **Integration tests**: Scheduled Tue/Thu 9am; block release if any fail.
- **E2E tests**: Run nightly; gate cases run Tue/Thu before release gate sign-off.
- **Regression suite**: Run on every build; smoke (fast subset) before every release candidate.

## Summary Table: Test Plan at a Glance

graders.evidence:
# Test Plan: Split Payment Feature (Release 5.3)

## 1. Context of Testing

**Scope**: Split Payment functionality enabling customers to pay a single order using two credit cards, with automatic refund of the first charge if the second charge is declined.

**Test Basis**: 
- Feature specification: split amount allocation (cents), two-card charge orchestration, 60-second refund SLA
- External PayGate payment gateway API
- Existing single-card checkout workflow (regression scope)

**Test Objectives**:
- Verify correct amount calculation and allocation (including remainder cent logic)
- Confirm both charges execute or fail safely
- Validate automatic refund completes within 60 seconds when second charge is declined
- Ensure single-card checkout remains functional (4,000 orders/day impact)
- Detect payment state machine defects (race conditions, incomplete transactions)

---

## 2. Assumptions and Constraints

| Assumption | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|
| Release deadline is 2026-11-13 (10 working days from today, 2026-10-28) | Explicit constraint |
| PayGate sandbox available Tuesdays and Thursdays only; no production testing | Explicit constraint; all integration tests scheduled for Tue/Thu windows |
| One tester at 50% FTE = ~50 hours available before release | 10 working days × 5 hours/day |
| Feature code is merged and compiles with zero errors at QA intake | Standard entry criterion |
| Test environment is QA-stage with PayGate sandbox credentials pre-configured | Deployment responsibility of DevOps; testing assumes ready state |
| Single-card payment code paths are unchanged (no refactor of existing logic) | Minimizes regression scope; if violated, regression suite grows |
| External PayGate API behavior is deterministic (no flaky responses in sandbox) | PayGate SLA assumption; if violated, test results become unreliable |
| Two developers remain available part-time for pairing on integration test execution | Developer involvement needed for API mock/stub setup and debugging |
| Refund automation is triggered server-side within the 60-second window; no manual intervention | Feature requirement interpretation |
| PCI compliance review has been completed separately (not in QA scope) | Assumption: security review is out of scope here |

---

## 3. Stakeholders

| Role | Responsibility | Relevance to Testing |
|------|-----------------|---------------------|
| **Product Owner** | Acceptance of release gate; sign-off on payment correctness | Owns correctness definition; reviews test results; approves go/no-go |
| **QA Lead (1 tester, 50% FTE)** | Test analysis, design, execution, defect reporting, risk tracking | Performs all testing activities; creates test cases; reports metrics daily |
| **Development Team (2 engineers)** | Implementation; PayGate integration; refund automation code | Pair on integration tests; debug failures; fix defects; owner of release gate sign-off |
| **DevOps / Infra** | Environment setup, PayGate sandbox access, QA deployment | Ensures test environment is ready before QA intake (entry criterion) |
| **PayGate Support** | API documentation, sandbox stability, incident response | External; escalation point for API failures; no direct testing role |

---

## 4. Communication

| Forum | Frequency | Participants | Content |
|-------|-----------|--------------|---------|
| Daily standup | 9:30 AM, weekdays | QA + 2 developers | Test progress, blockers, PayGate availability window conflicts |
| Risk review meeting | Every 2 working days (Mon, Wed) | QA Lead + PO + dev lead | Re-score risk register, move cases into/out of release gate, escalate blockers |
| End-of-day summary | 5 PM, weekdays | QA + PO (async) | Test execution count, defects opened/closed, regression status |
| PayGate availability alert | Tue/Thu mornings | QA team | Confirm sandbox is live; schedule integration test windows |
| Final readiness review | Day before release (2026-11-12) | QA Lead, Dev Lead, PO | Release gate execution, defect status, sign-off decision |

**Document Templates**:
- Daily test log: test case ID, status (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED), defect link, evidence (screenshots for failures)
- Defect report: severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), reproducible steps, expected vs. actual, PayGate API response (if applicable)
- Risk register: updated in-place with dated corrections (no deletion of prior scores)

---

## 5. Risk Register (5×5 Product & Project Risk Matrix)

| # | ID | Risk Description | Category | L | I | Score | Level | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status |
|---|----|--------------------|----------|---|---|-------|---------|----------------------|-------|--------|
| 1 | R01 | Amount split calculation error (e.g., remainder cent logic inverted) | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Unit test 100% of split scenarios; code review by 2nd developer; table-driven tests for edge cases (0.01 split) | Dev + QA | To do |
| 2 | R02 | First charge succeeds, second charge fails → no automatic refund or delayed refund | Product | 3 | 5 | 15 | 🔴 CRITICAL | Automate refund flow with E2E test; monitor server logs for refund completion time; set PayGate webhook timeout to 30s (half of 60s SLA); integration test with PayGate sandbox (Tue/Thu only) | Dev + QA | To do |
| 3 | R03 | Both charges fail silently or user is not notified of payment status | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | Test error handling for all PayGate decline codes; verify UI shows error message for each scenario; integration test with PayGate sandbox | QA | To do |
| 4 | R04 | Single-card checkout regression: new code breaks existing 4,000 orders/day flow | Product | 2 | 5 | 10 | 🟠 HIGH | Run existing single-card regression suite (all 30+ cases); smoke test on QA after deployment; monitor UAT for anomalies | QA | To do |
| 5 | R05 | Race condition: user submits refund request while first charge refund is in-flight | Product | 1 | 4 | 4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Idempotency testing: submit same refund request twice, verify refund happens only once; integration test with stubs for timing control | Dev | To do |
| 6 | R06 | PayGate sandbox unavailable or returns unexpected API responses | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | PayGate sandbox confirmed available Tue/Thu only (hard constraint); schedule all integration tests within windows; fallback: use PayGate API mocks/stubs for non-Tue/Thu testing | Dev + QA | To do |
| 7 | R07 | Test execution time overruns 50 available hours; release gate cases not completed in time | Project | 3 | 4 | 12 | 🟠 HIGH | Prioritize release gate first; automate regression suite to run in parallel (single-card tests); defer exploratory testing to post-release if time is tight; daily stand-up tracking | QA | To do |
| 8 | R08 | Payment state machine in inconsistent state (e.g., first charge marked refunded but second charge never attempted) | Product | 2 | 4 | 8 | 🟠 HIGH | State transition testing: verify all state paths through decision table (success, fail card1, fail card2, timeout); integration test with controlled PayGate delays | Dev + QA | To do |
| 9 | R09 | Refund completes outside 60-second SLA (e.g., PayGate is slow or network latency) | Product | 2 | 3 | 6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Measure refund completion time in integration tests; set PayGate sandbox timeout to 30s; log timestamps at each stage (charge1, charge2, refund start, refund end) | QA | To do |
| 10 | R10 | PCI compliance issue in new payment code paths (credential storage, logging) | Product | 1 | 5 | 5 | 🟡 MEDIUM | Code review checklist for PCI DSS compliance (no card data in logs, no storage); security team sign-off (out of QA scope but logged here for traceability) | Security + Dev | To do |

---

## 6. Test Approach

### Test Levels & Types

**Unit Testing (40% of effort)**
- **Scope**: Amount calculation logic, validation, edge cases
- **Techniques**: Equivalence partitioning (valid splits, edge amounts), boundary value analysis (0.01 splits, integer + remainder), decision tables (all paths through split logic)
- **Independence**: Developer (author) with peer review; QA reviews test cases post-writing
- **Deliverables**: Test cases for split amount calculation, remainder cent logic, validation errors
- **Entry Criteria**: Feature code merged, compiles, zero lint errors
- **Exit Criteria**: 100% coverage of split logic paths; all cases passing

**Integration Testing (35% of effort)**
- **Scope**: Payment orchestration, PayGate API calls, refund automation, state machine
- **Techniques**: State transition testing (all charge/refund sequences), API contract testing (PayGate request/response validation), error injection (declined cards, timeouts)
- **Independence**: Developers with QA pairing; QA designs and executes test cases
- **Deliverables**: Test cases for refund flow, charge sequences, PayGate API interactions, error scenarios
- **Entry Criteria**: Unit tests passing; PayGate sandbox credentials configured; test data seeded
- **Exit Criteria**: Release gate cases passing; all charge/refund scenarios validated

**System & E2E Testing (25% of effort)**
- **Scope**: Full split payment user journey (UI → checkout → two-card entry → charges → success/error display), regression on single-card flow
- **Techniques**: User scenario testing (happy path, error path), exploratory testing (UI edge cases, back-button behavior), regression testing (existing checkout)
- **Independence**: QA (high independence); developers available for debugging
- **Deliverables**: Test cases for split payment UX, regression suite for single-card, exploratory findings log
- **Entry Criteria**: Integration tests passing; QA environment deployed; test users configured
- **Exit Criteria**: Release gate cases passing; single-card regression suite 100% passing

### Test Execution Order (Risk-Based)

1. **Release gate cases** (first): 8 critical cases (see Release Gate table below) → must pass before release
2. **High-risk integration tests** (parallel with gate): R02 (refund automation) and R04 (single-card regression) cases
3. **Unit tests** (as needed): Support for gate case failures
4. **Exploratory testing** (if time permits): Edge cases, boundary conditions
5. **Post-release retesting** (if defects found): Confirmation on fixed defects

**Constraints overriding order**:
- PayGate sandbox available Tue/Thu only → integration tests scheduled within these windows
- Developers' availability for pairing → schedule integration test sessions with both devs confirmed

### Test Basis & Traceability

- Feature specification (split amount logic, refund SLA)
- PayGate API documentation (charge, refund endpoints)
- Single-card checkout regression suite (existing test cases)
- Risk register (R01–R10 drive test case selection)

### Release Gate (Go/No-Go Criteria)

**Definition**: Minimum set of 8 cases that answer "do the fixes work?" and "did the change break existing checkout?"

| # | Gate Case ID | Test Scenario | Expected Result | Automation | Owner |
|---|---------------|--------|-----------------|------------|-------|
| G1 | TC-SP-001 | Split $100.00: $60 on card 1, $40 on card 2; both cards valid | Both charges succeed; order total matches | E2E automated | QA |
| G2 | TC-SP-002 | Split $100.01: $60 on card 1, $40.01 on card 2; remainder cent on card 1 (validates logic) | First charge $60.01, second $40; order total $100.01 | Integration (PayGate API) | Dev + QA |
| G3 | TC-SP-003 | Split $50.00: card 1 valid, card 2 declined | First charge succeeds, refund initiated; order marked failed; customer sees error | Integration + E2E | QA |
| G4 | TC-SP-004 | Refund on G3 completes within 60 seconds | Refund timestamp − charge1 timestamp ≤ 60s; PayGate returns refund success | Integration (mocked PayGate delay testing) | Dev + QA |
| G5 | TC-SP-005 | Single-card payment $100 (regression): existing checkout not broken | Charge succeeds; order placed; same behavior as pre-release | E2E automated (existing test) | QA |
| G6 | TC-SP-006 | Split UI displays: split amount inputs, currency, card selector | Both card fields visible, placeholders correct, no UI errors | E2E automated | QA |
| G7 | TC-SP-007 | Both cards declined: card 1 and card 2 both fail | Error shown; no charges made; no refund attempted | Integration + E2E | QA |
| G8 | TC-SP-008 | Edge case: split $0.01 (1¢ on card 1, $0 on card 2) | Card 1 charged $0.01, card 2 not charged; order succeeds | Unit + Integration | Dev |

**Gate Pass/Fail Decision**: Release approved only if ALL 8 cases PASS and zero Critical-severity defects open. If any gate case fails, defect is logged, fixed, and case re-executed before release decision.

### Entry & Exit Criteria

**Entry Criteria for System Testing** (when to START):
- [ ] Split payment feature code merged to QA branch with zero compilation/linting errors
- [ ] All unit tests passing locally (developer verification)
- [ ] QA environment deployed and accessible
- [ ] PayGate sandbox credentials configured and verified (test charge succeeds)
- [ ] Test data (test card numbers, amounts) prepared and seeded
- [ ] Single-card checkout regression test suite extracted and ready to run
- [ ] Risk register reviewed and signed by QA Lead and Dev Lead

**Exit Criteria for Release** (when to STOP and release):
- [ ] All 8 release gate cases executed and PASSING
- [ ] Single-card regression suite (30+ cases) executed and 100% PASSING
- [ ] Zero Critical-severity defects open
- [ ] Zero High-severity defects open, OR each High defect has a documented Product Owner exception
- [ ] Refund automation tested and confirmed: refund completes ≤ 60 seconds in 3+ test runs
- [ ] Test summary report signed by QA Lead and Product Owner
- [ ] Configuration management checklist complete (see item 9 below)

---

## 7. Test Effort Estimation

**Technique**: Expert-based, three-point estimation (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic)

**Formula**: E = (a + 4m + b) / 6; SD = (b − a) / 6

### Breakdown by Activity

| Activity | a (opt, hrs) | m (likely, hrs) | b (pess, hrs) | E (hrs) | SD (hrs) | Risk Drivers |
|----------|--------|----------|---------|--------|---------|--------------|
| Unit test design & execution | 6 | 9 | 14 | 9.3 | 1.3 | Amount logic complexity, edge cases |
| Integration test design & execution | 10 | 16 | 22 | 16.0 | 2.0 | PayGate sandbox availability (Tue/Thu only), state machine paths |
| E2E & UI test design & execution | 8 | 12 | 16 | 12.0 | 1.3 | UI interaction flakiness, screenshot capture |
| Single-card regression execution | 6 | 9 | 12 | 9.0 | 1.0 | Existing test suite size, environment stability |
| Defect investigation & retesting | 4 | 5 | 8 | 5.3 | 0.7 | Defect complexity, fix turnaround time |
| **Total** | **34** | **51** | **72** | **51.6** | **6.3** | — |

**Estimate Summary**:
- **Point Estimate**: 51.6 hours
- **Range**: 34–72 hours (with 95% confidence: 51.6 ± 2×6.3 = 38.8–64.2 hours)
- **Available Time**: 50 hours (1 tester, 50% FTE, 10 working days × 5 hrs/day)
- **Slack**: −1.6 hours (tight; exploratory testing deferred if overrun)

**Assumptions underpinning estimate**:
- Developers available 4 hours/week for pairing on integration tests (already factored)
- PayGate sandbox is stable and available on all Tue/Thu windows within the release window
- No additional compliance or security reviews required by QA
- Single-card regression suite is already documented and does not require redesign
- Defect fix turnaround is 24 hours (same-day for Critical)

---

## 8. Budget & Schedule

**Timeline**:
- **Start Date**: Monday, 2026-10-28
- **Release Date**: Wednesday, 2026-11-13 (10 working days)
- **PayGate Sandbox Windows**: Tue 2026-10-29, Thu 2026-10-31, Tue 2026-11-05, Thu 2026-11-07, Tue 2026-11-12 (5 windows available)

**Schedule** (50 hours QA + dev pairing):

| Week | Day | Focus | Hours | Notes |
|------|-----|-------|-------|-------|
| W1 | Mon 10-28 | Test plan finalization, risk review, unit test case design | 5 | Parallel: dev starts coding |
| W1 | Tue 10-29 | Unit test execution (live PayGate window) | 5 | 1st integration test prep |
| W1 | Wed 10-30 | Unit test completion, integration test design | 4 | 1 hr buffer for overruns |
| W1 | Thu 10-31 | Integration tests on PayGate sandbox (live window) | 5 | 2 devs pair; test refund automation |
| W1 | Fri 11-01 | Defect investigation, single-card regression suite setup | 5 | Release gate case results review |
| W2 | Mon 11-04 | Single-card regression execution (start) | 5 | — |
| W2 | Tue 11-05 | Integration tests (live PayGate window), regression continuation | 5 | Refund E2E tests |
| W2 | Wed 11-06 | E2E split payment tests, exploratory testing (if time) | 4 | 1 hr buffer |
| W2 | Thu 11-07 | Release gate re-test if failures found (live PayGate window) | 5 | Final defect fix verification |
| W2 | Fri 11-08 | Regression completion, test summary report | 5 | — |
| W2 | Mon 11-11 | Final readiness review, risk re-scoring | 1 | Holiday consideration (Veterans Day in US; may affect availability) |
| W2 | Tue 11-12 | Final smoke testing (if live PayGate window available) | 1 | Day before release |
| | | **Total** | **50** | QA allocation only; dev pairing adds ~8 hrs |

**Resources**:
- QA Lead (tester): 1 FTE at 50% = 5 hrs/day, 10 working days = **50 hours**
- Dev Team (2 engineers): Pairing for ~2 hrs/session, 4 sessions = **8 hours** (shared with implementation)
- DevOps: Environment deployment (pre-QA intake), PayGate sandbox access (assumed pre-configured)
- PayGate Support: Escalation only; no billable time expected

**Budget Allocation** (if hourly):
- QA hours: 50 @ \$75/hr = \$3,750
- Dev pairing: 8 @ \$100/hr = \$800
- **Total QA+Dev**: \$4,550
- **Contingency** (10%): \$455
- **Total Budget**: ~\$5,000

---

## 9. Configuration Management of Testware

**Identification & Version Control**:
- Test plan, test cases, test results, and risk register stored in project repository at `/qa/split-payment/`
- Naming convention: `TC-SP-NNN` (test case ID), `RG-SP-NNN` (risk ID), `DEF-SP-NNN` (defect ID)
- All artifacts versioned in Git with commit messages referencing issue tracker IDs (e.g., `JIRA-1234`)
- Test case changes require Pull Request with dev + QA sign-off

**Baseline Environments** (reproducibility):
- **QA-Stage**: PayGate sandbox (Tue/Thu only); QA database snapshot taken at test start; tagged in environment config
- **All test results must include**:
  - Build version (commit hash)
  - Environment name and timestamp
  - PayGate sandbox API version used
  - Screenshots or video (for E2E failures)
  - PayGate API request/response logs (truncated for security; no card data)

**Restoring Baselines**:
- QA database reset script: `qa/scripts/reset-test-db.sql` (idempotent; can be re-run)
- Test data (test card numbers): loaded from secure config file (not in repo; reference only)
- PayGate sandbox state: reset via PayGate API call before each test session

**CI/CD Integration**:
- Unit and integration test suites run in GitHub Actions on every push to QA branch (pass/fail gate)
- E2E tests run nightly on QA-Stage environment (not in-PR, due to PayGate sandbox availability)
- Release gate cases tagged `@release-gate` in test framework; separate CI job reports status

**Traceability Matrix**:
- Risk → Test Case: Each risk (R01–R10) linked to 1+ test case(s); see Risk Register column "Mitigation Strategy"
- Test Case → Test Result: Each TC linked to its execution result (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED with defect ID if failed)
- Defect → Fix: Each DEF linked to code commit(s) that fix it, and linked back to TC that caught it

**Test Data Management**:
- Fixture set document at `/qa/split-payment/test-data.md`:
  - Test card numbers (valid, declined, timeout scenarios) — reference only, no card data in plaintext
  - Test amounts ($0.01, $100.00, $100.01 edge cases)
  - PayGate sandbox merchant ID and API keys (stored in secure config, not in repo)
  - Refund test scenarios (card1 success + card2 decline → refund expected)

**Handover & Resumption**:
- If testing is paused/resumed, mark the stopping point in test log: "Last executed: TC-SP-005 on 2026-11-06 14:30. Next: TC-SP-006 (E2E UI test)."
- All open defects remain in tracker (not deleted); each linked to the test case that found it and the commit that fixes it
- Risk register corrections dated in-place: "Updated R02 likelihood 3→2 on 2026-11-05 per dev confirmation of refund timeout margin."

---

## Key Dependencies & Risks Summary

**Critical Path** (items that can delay release if not met):
1. PayGate sandbox availability (Tue/Thu only) — 5 windows in the release window
2. Developers' availability for integration test pairing (4 hrs/week committed)
3. Refund automation completion time < 60s (functional requirement; must pass gate)
4. Single-card regression suite execution time (must fit in 50-hour budget)

**Escalation Triggers**:
- Any Critical defect found after Wed 2026-11-06 → stop release and re-plan
- PayGate sandbox unavailable on any Tue/Thu → escalate to dev team for mock/stub solution
- Test execution time exceeds 50 hours by end of Fri 2026-11-08 → defer exploratory testing, release on gate cases only
- Defect fix turnaround > 24 hours → assign additional dev resource or de-scope feature from this release
